☆ Unbounded DiPerna-Lions commutators for Osgood-Sobolev vector fields
Leonardo Franchi, Carl Johan Peter Johansson
In this paper we show that there exists a regime of Osgood-Sobolev vector fields in which the DiPerna-Lions scheme cannot be applied despite the recently proved well-posedness and propagation of regularity in arXiv:2607.28118. For Osgood-Sobolev vector fields we also show that the propagation of regularity proved in arXiv:2607.28118 is sharp and derive lower bounds on mixing.
☆ Strong Ill-Posedness for the Surface Quasi-Geostrophic Equations in $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$
Elaine Cozzi, Nicholas Harrison, Zachary Radke
We establish ill-posedness of the surface quasi-geostrophic equations in Sobolev spaces $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ for every integer $k \geq 3$. This includes the scaling critical space $W^{3,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. We build on ideas from (arXiv:2610.04872); in particular, we use a theorem of Bonami and Poornima to construct a basic building block, or packet, which obeys a linear evolution approximating that of the perturbation of the background solution to SQG. The Bonami-Poornima theorem ensures that this packet has both small initial $W^{k,1}$ norm and large $W^{k,1}$ norm at positive times. We then implement a process known as many packet dilution, which allows one to construct an initial perturbation as a sum of sufficiently many packets to dilute the effect of the nonlinear term. This initial perturbation leads to the desired norm inflation. To establish instantaneous blow-up of the $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ norm, we also prove a local well-posedness result in the critical Sobolev-Lorentz space $W^{2,(2,1)}(\mathbb{R}^2)$. This result gives a uniform lower bound on the existence time for solutions with bounded $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ data, even though the solutions' $W^{k,1}(\mathbb{R}^2)$ norms may become arbitrarily large in arbitrarily short time.

☆ Oleinik estimate for a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit
Boris Haspot, Animesh Jana
In this article, we establish an Oleinik type estimate for $2\times2$ systems of hyperbolic conservation laws in a class of Temple systems via vanishing viscosity limit. More precisely, we consider the parabolic approximation with vanishing viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon u_{xx}$ ($\varepsilon>0$) for the Temple class of hyperbolic system of conservation laws and for these approximate solutions we obtain an Oleinik type estimate uniformly with respect to the viscosity coefficient $\varepsilon>0$. This extends the Oleinik inequality for scalar conservation laws with viscosity to the system. Subsequently, we prove that these approximate solutions converge via the process of vanishing viscosity limit to a global weak solution of the limit strictly hyperbolic system provided that the initial data is small in $L^\infty$. To do this we implement the vanishing viscosity method of Bianchini and Bressan [Indiana Univ. Math. J. 2000] with $L^\infty$ initial data which requires new tools as an local in time Oleinik estimate (obtained by employing a suitable maximum principle and a normal form argument) and a localization argument. In particular we need to introduce appropriate weight functions which satisfy a Bellman equation to get new localized transversal interaction estimates.
☆ A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere
Ali Barki, Shubham Gupta, Yaozhong W. Qiu
We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(Δ+ 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |ξ|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 dξ,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

☆ Numerical analysis of a conservative Crank-Nicolson scheme for quasilinear Gross-Pitaevskii equations
Sebastián Tapia-Mandiola
We propose and analyze a fully discrete Crank-Nicolson finite-difference scheme for one-dimensional quasilinear Hamiltonian Gross-Pitaevskii equations with homogeneous Neumann boundary conditions. We establish the existence and uniqueness of numerical solutions and an $H^1$-stability estimate. For sufficiently regular exact solutions, we obtain second-order convergence in both time and space in the discrete $H^1$-norm. The analysis covers the focusing and defocusing cubic nonlinearities and both signs of the quasilinear coefficient $κ$, under a uniform discrete ellipticity condition when $κ<0$. The main difficulty in the error analysis comes from the derivatives introduced by the quasilinear interaction. To overcome this problem, we introduce a discrete action combining the discrete energy and mass, and establish a coercivity inequality in the discrete $H^1$-norm that allows us to control the numerical error. Together with consistency estimates and a discrete Gronwall inequality, this yields second-order convergence. Numerical experiments with bright solitons corroborate the predicted convergence rates.
☆ Boundary Observability for a Class of Degenerate Kolmogorov-Type Equations in a Cylindrical Domain
Dong-Hui Yang, Mengze Gu, Yuanzhi Zhou, Ghadir Shokor
This paper investigates the boundary observability for a class of multi-dimensional degenerate Kolmogorov-type kinetic equations in a cylindrical domain $Ω= \mathbb{T}_{x_1} \times (0,1)_{x_2}$. The model features a horizontal drift term $x_2^γ\partial_{x_1} \varphi$ coupled with a boundary-degenerate diffusion operator $\partial_{x_2}(x_2^α\partial_{x_2} \varphi)$ acting solely on the velocity variable, where $γ= 1$ and $α\in (0,1)$. By leveraging the structural advantages of the cylindrical domain, we establish an analytical framework based on the method of separation of variables. Crucial Carleman estimates tailored to the degenerate dual operator are derived to capture the subtle dissipation effects under the influence of the transport term. Consequently, by virtue of a uniform a priori estimate, we establish the quantitative boundary observability inequality for the state function.
☆ Sharp entanglement and decay thresholds for fractional elliptic operators
Yi-Hsuan Lin, Hongyu Liu
We establish sharp entanglement principles for fractional powers of uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators $L$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$, $n\ge 2$, with smooth real symmetric coefficients. Let $u_1,\ldots,u_N$ and the sum $\sum_{k=1}^N L^{s_k}u_k$ vanish on a common nonempty open set. Assuming that $L$ coincides with the Laplacian outside a compact set, we prove that root-exponential decay of these functions forces every $u_k$ to vanish globally, under sharp dimension-dependent conditions on the fractional orders $s_k$. The exponent $1/2$ is optimal within the stretched-exponential scale, and the sharp logarithmic endpoint is $e^{-a\sqrt{r}/\log r}$ in every dimension. Our approach relies on a novel resolvent characterization of entanglement, which we use both to separate the fractional orders at zero energy and to construct exact cancellations from outgoing waves. For perturbations extending to infinity, this wave construction yields two-dimensional counterexamples with smooth compactly supported inputs and coefficient fields converging to the identity in every fixed unweighted $C^k$ norm. Finally, for a known underlying operator, a single exterior measurement determines the number, orders, and coefficients of the fractional terms, together with a continuous potential.

☆ A second-order relaxation system for a degenerate-parabolic quasilinear fourth-order rimming-flow equation with critical spectrum
Rahul Barthwal, Juri Joussen, Christina Lienstromberg, Christian Rohde
For a spectrally critical nonlinear degenerate-parabolic PDE of fourth-order, describing a capillary-driven fluid flow in a rotating cylinder, we propose a second-order relaxation system of parabolic-elliptic type. For positive initial data, we prove local existence and uniqueness of solutions to the relaxation system. Thereby, the lifespan of the approximate solutions turns out to be independent of the relaxation parameter. Moreover, we prove convergence of non-negative weak solutions of the relaxation system to weak solutions of the original equation on compact time intervals. We classify positive steady states of the relaxed system, prove a stability result yielding global strong solutions, and show that the long-time dynamics remain consistent under the relaxation limit.

☆ Gravitational collapse to extremal black holes with $Λ>0$: counterexamples to the third law without charge
Mónica Tapia del Moral
We study the dynamical formation of the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution, in both its time orientations, and the related Nariai solution. We prove that there exist spherically symmetric, regular Cauchy data for the Einstein-scalar field system with $\mathbb S^3$ topology, for any scalar field mass $\mathfrak{m}\geq 0$, that lead to the formation of an exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter black hole in finite time, and that moreover the apparent horizon of the solution is exactly isometric to that of the subextremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter solution at earlier times. We also show that if the scalar field mass satisfies $\mathfrak{m}>\sqrtΛ/2$, an analogous result holds having the extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter white hole or the Nariai solution in place of the black hole. In the black hole case, the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region is bounded to the future by two event horizons and can be seen as the analogue of the exterior region in the asymptotically flat case. We moreover establish that these two black hole horizons that bound the exactly extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region are the only event horizons present in the spacetime, something non-trivial given the existence of multi-black hole configurations when $Λ> 0$. Consequently, the solutions arising from these data can be thought to constitute, in particular, regular counterexamples to the third law of black hole thermodynamics with $Λ>0$ arising from the collapse of physically plausible matter which is moreover uncharged. Our approach to construct the Cauchy data relies on $C^k$ characteristic gluing results for the Einstein-scalar field system in spherical symmetry, in the spirit of [KU25].

☆ Viscosity solutions for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms
Russell Schwab, Son N. T. Tu, Olga Turanova
We address global well-posedness for integro-differential equations with gradient and source terms. This naturally results from establishing the comparison principle for viscosity solutions and existence via Perron's method. There are many earlier results for similar equations, and our work attempts to give a unified approach and improve upon some recent examples. There is a natural juxtaposition of earlier results in the usual framework of viscosity solutions which rely on a min-max structure, with some more recent implementations coming from the free boundary literature in which a min-max is not apparent initially, but does appear a posteriori due to certain rigid structural constraints. Here we give a presentation that combines ideas from both situations. The most important feature of the operators in our equations is what we call the global comparison property. This is combined with a natural local Lipschitz assumption on the operator defining the equation.

☆ Existence of odd-frequency free boundary points in the Signorini problem
Xavier Fernández-Real
Up to a lower-dimensional set, the free boundary of the Signorini problem consists of points with frequency that is half-integer, even (at zero density points), or odd (at full density points). Surprisingly, despite extensive work on the structure and regularity of each of these sets, the existence of odd-frequency free boundary points has remained open. ☆ Global Convergence of Second-Order Methods for Physics-Informed Neural Networks in the Overparameterized Limit
Konstantin Riedl, Justin Sirignano, Konstantinos Spiliopoulos
Solving high-dimensional partial differential equations (PDEs) constitutes a core task in many engineering and scientific disciplines. Physics-informed neural networks and the deep Galerkin method effectively leverage machine learning models to approximate solutions of known PDEs by minimizing residuals corresponding to the PDE operator alongside external constraints. Although second-order optimizers are becoming increasingly popular for training neural networks (NNs) to solve PDEs and empirically outperform their first-order counterparts in both speed and accuracy, the convergence theory for training such models is essentially confined to first-order methods. In this paper, we close this gap and develop a convergence analysis for the regularized Newton and Gauss-Newton methods. As the number of hidden units tends to infinity, the training dynamics converge in probability, with explicit rates, to the solution of a deterministic limit equation involving a Newton neural tangent kernel operator associated with the PDE. Although the limiting kernel operator admits no spectral gap, we prove that, in the overparameterized limit, the PDE residual vanishes as training proceeds, and, under mild assumptions, the NN converges to the PDE solution. We further show that, provided a sufficiently small regularization parameter, the projection of the residual onto any fixed number of leading eigenfunctions decays exponentially fast, demonstrating that this hyperparameter acts as a spectral filter: it lifts the convergence rates of high-frequency components toward those of low-frequency ones, thereby mitigating the spectral bias inherent in gradient descent. Mathematical challenges arise from the implicit parameter update involving a linear system whose dimension increases with the NN width and, for Newton's method, a potentially indefinite Hessian, as well as from the PDE operator entering the kernel.

☆ Prandtl Batchelor flow in a Periodic Channel with Counter Moving Walls
Zeyu Jia, Tao Tao
We study the vanishing viscosity limit of steady two dimensional incompressible Navier Stokes flows in a horizontally periodic channel with counter moving walls. The prescribed wall velocities are small periodic perturbations of constant velocities with opposite signs. The Batchelor Wood relations select an affine Euler shear with constant vorticity and a unique interior zero. We establish the existence of steady Navier Stokes solutions that are uniformly approximated by the selected Euler shear together with two Prandtl boundary layers. Moreover, the vorticity converges locally uniformly to the selected constant vorticity. The principal analytical difficulty is the loss of global coercivity caused by the interior zero of the Euler shear. To overcome this difficulty, we develop a compactness rigidity argument that combines signed near wall positivity estimates, interior vorticity estimates, adjoint tests eliminating the affine limiting modes, and a streamline circulation equation ruling out concentration near the walls. These ingredients yield an estimate for the linearized inverse, which, together with a high order Euler Prandtl approximation, enables us to solve the nonlinear error equations. Our result provides a rigorous realization of the Prandtl Batchelor selection principle in a periodic channel with counter moving walls.
☆ The singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds: refined blow-up analysis and degree jumps
Mohameden Ahmedou, Lina Wu, Lei Zhang
We compute the Leray--Schauder degree of the singular Paneitz equation on a closed four-manifold with conical orders strictly between minus one and zero. We assume that the kernel of the Paneitz operator consists of the constants. In each positive nonresonant chamber the degree is a partial sum of an explicit generating series determined by the Euler characteristic and the conical orders. We match the heights of exact blow-up solutions and expand the gradient near the corrected projected bubbles. A localized dilation identity gives its common-scale component on the zero set of the relative-scale equations. For generic data a fixed-mass homotopy then gives the signed degree of each concentrating configuration. Assign ordinary points weight one and conical points weight one plus their order. If the largest concentrating weight exceeds one half, a finite second moment gives the coefficient. At one half the expansion acquires a logarithm, and below one half the coefficient is a global finite part. On the round four-sphere with two antipodal points of equal weight below one half, perturbing the prescribed curvature away from both points selects the side of bubbling.

Michael Eden
We study a diffusion problem in a highly heterogeneous periodic medium (characterized by a small scale parameter $0<\varepsilon\ll1$) where small inclusions are separated from the surrounding connected area by solute-impermeable membranes. These membranes are allowed to grow and deform under surface tension and osmotic pressure (driven by the concentration difference across the membrane). We prove existence of weak solutions on a time interval which is independent of the microscopic scale via a Schauder fixed-point argument by establishing spatial boundary Hölder estimates. For the homogenization limit $\varepsilon\to0$, we establish strong compactness of the outer concentration via time translates and then derive a stability estimate for the driven inner cell problems. ☆ Morse theory and a degree formula for the resonant singular Paneitz equation on four-manifolds
Mohameden Ahmedou, Lina Wu, Lei Zhang
We develop Morse theory for the singular Paneitz equation at resonant mass on closed four-manifolds with conical orders between minus one and zero and Paneitz kernel consisting of the constants. Under nondegeneracy of the reduced interactions and nonvanishing of the leading mass-defect coefficients, we classify the critical points at infinity by the sign of these coefficients. We compute their indices and their contributions to the relative homology of sublevels. The topology of very low sublevels is determined by weighted barycenters of strictly smaller total weight and by the negative Paneitz eigenspace. These results yield strong Morse inequalities and a Leray--Schauder degree formula at resonance, which also applies when genuine solutions are degenerate. ☆ Mean field game value multifunction: dynamic programming principle
Y. Averboukh, S. Mayorga
We study mean field games (MFGs) on the torus with non-degenerate diffusion, in a regime (no monotonicity) where multiple solutions exist for the same data. In this setting the value of a representative player is not a function of the initial time and distribution, and the classical master equation loses its meaning. We describe the dependence of the value on the initial data by a multivalued mapping, the value multifunction, assigning to each initial time and distribution the set of value functions of all solutions of the MFG starting from that data. Our main result gives a sufficient condition for a closed multifunction to be a value multifunction, namely, it must satisfy a dynamic programming principle formulated on proper time subintervals, expressed as invariance of its graph under the forward operators generated by equilibria of the game. This replaces the global requirement that each value be produced by a solution of the forward-backward system on the whole time interval by a local, time-consistent condition together with closedness, which carries the terminal condition. The result is the second-order analogue of the viability approach previously developed for first-order mean field games. We reformulate solutions of the mean field game in terms of relaxed equilibria, show that the closure of a value multifunction is again a value multifunction, and prove that the forward operators compose as a semigroup. We also present an explicit example in which a single terminal cost produces at least two solutions for every initial time in an interval, while solutions are unique for initial times sufficiently close to the horizon.

We propose and analyse a structure-preserving discretization of the fourth-order DLSS equation in dynamically rescaled variables leading to a linear confinement on the one-dimensional real line. ☆ Reconstruction of Poisson Random Measures in the Variational Framework with Applications to Jump-Driven SPDEs
Erika Hausenblas, Akash Ashirbad Panda, Ankit Kumar
We establish a reconstruction principle for Poisson random measures arising in compactness arguments for jump-driven stochastic partial differential equations. A basic difficulty in such arguments is that, after a Skorokhod-type representation, almost sure convergence of the solution processes does not by itself identify the limiting stochastic integral, since integration with respect to a compensated Poisson random measure is not a pathwise continuous functional of the solution and the noise. We address this problem in the variational framework of a Gelfand triple $V\hookrightarrow H\equiv H^\ast\hookrightarrow V^\ast$ for equations with locally monotone drift. Starting from a tight sequence of approximating solutions in $D([0,T];H)\cap L^α(0,T;V),$ we construct, on the represented probability space, a time-homogeneous Poisson random measure with the original Lévy intensity and compensator, compatible with the limiting filtration, such that the limiting process solves the corresponding SPDE. The main ingredient is a noise bridge. Together with a shifted dyadic approximation of the solution, the increments of the solution path over dyadic time cells approximate the compensated noise increments; since the time integral of the drift is continuous in $H$, no regularisation of the drift is needed. The jumps are then recovered by a measurable registration procedure, while injectivity of the jump coefficient permits reconstruction of the corresponding marks through a Borel inverse obtained from the Lusin--Suslin theorem. The reconstruction is performed simultaneously at all truncation levels; consistency of the resulting finite jump measures and a monotone patching argument yield a Poisson random measure with the full Lévy measure. Under the injectivity assumption, no enlargement of the represented probability space is required.

☆ Existence and nonexistence results for a mixed local--nonlocal operator with a Hardy potential
Boumediene Abdellaoui, Kheireddine Biroud, El-Haj Laamri, Luigi Montoro
We investigate a class of problems involving the mixed local-nonlocal operator $-Δ+(-Δ)^s$, with $s\in(0,1)$, and a Hardy-type potential, in a bounded smooth domain $Ω\subset\mathbb{R}^N$, $N\geq 3$, containing the origin. The problem involves a positive parameter $λ$ and a nonnegative measurable function $f$ satisfying suitable assumptions. We first study the associated linear problem with a prescribed datum. By means of a suitable change of variables and within an appropriate framework of weighted Sobolev spaces, we establish a weak Harnack inequality for the resulting weighted mixed operator. As a consequence, we derive the precise asymptotic behavior of nonnegative solutions near the singularity at the origin, and we obtain a necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of weak solutions. We then address the nonlinear case for two classes of nonlinearities, namely $f(x,u)=u^q+g(x)$ and $f(x,u)=h(x)/u^σ$. For the first class, we identify a critical exponent governing the existence of solutions; for the second, we establish existence results for a broad class of data $h$.
☆ Kelvin-invariant positive solutions for critical elliptic systems with repulsive interaction
Yohei Sato, Reo Suzuki
In this paper, we consider the following critical nonlinear elliptic system with repulsive interaction: \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{ll} -Δu_1 = μ_1 u_1^3 - β(x) u_1 u_2^2 & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^4, \cr -Δu_2 = μ_2 u_2^3 - β(x) u_1^2 u_2 & \text{in } \mathbb{R}^4, \cr u_1, u_2 \in \mathcal{D}^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^4), & \end{array} \right. \] where $μ_1, μ_2 > 0$ and $β(x) \in C(\mathbb{R}^4,\mathbb{R})$ is a nonnegative function. Assuming that $β$ is invariant under the map $x \mapsto -\frac{x}{\vert{}x\vert{}^2}$, we establish the existence of positive solutions to $(\mathcal{P}_β)$ that are invariant under the Kelvin transform subject to suitable assumptions. This result provides a critical counterpart to the work of Sato [Y. Sato, Nonlinear Anal. 234 (2023), 113302], who established the existence of an even ground state for the corresponding subcritical problem. Furthermore, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the obtained solutions as $\|β\|_\infty \to 0$.

☆ Multiple positive solutions near segregated profiles in Lotka-Volterra competition systems with asymmetric interactions
Zaizheng Li, Susanna Terracini
We consider stationary Lotka--Volterra competition-diffusion systems with any number of species and positive, possibly asymmetric competition coefficients. We study two settings with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions: a one-dimensional interval with constant drift, and radial solutions on a ball. In each setting we first determine when a prescribed ordering of species admits a segregated profile. Starting from such a profile, we construct a positive solution for every sufficiently large competition parameter $β$. The uniform distance from the profile is of order $\varepsilon=β^{-1/3}$, and the rescaled densities converge near each interface to a two-species model. Counting the admissible orderings gives a lower bound on the number of positive solutions. We also prove a non-approximation result when one directed competition coefficient is zero and the other species are suppressed on the interval or shell used in the proof.

☆ Global existence of small data solutions to 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equations, II

For the 3-D semilinear Euler-Poisson-Darboux equation $\square u+\fracμ{t}\partial_tu=|u|^p$, where $t\geq1$, $μ>0$ and $p>1$, it is conjectured that the small data solution $u$ exists globally when $p>p_s(3+μ)=\frac{μ+4+\sqrt{μ^2+16μ+32}}{2(μ+2)}$ for $0<μ\le \frac{14}{5}$, and when $p>p_f(3)=\frac{5}{3}$ for $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$, where $p_s$ and $p_f$ denote the Strauss and Fujita exponents, respectively. Preprint (2026), arXiv:2607.04575], for $p>\max\{\frac{5}{3},1+\frac{2}μ\}$ and $μ\geq\frac{14}{5}$, the global small solution $u$ was obtained. ☆ Scattering for the defocusing two-dimensional NLS with an Aharonov-Bohm magnetic potential
Luca Fanelli, Vladimir Georgiev, Sandra Lucente, Nicola Visciglia
We study the defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation in two dimensions in the presence of an Aharonov--Bohm magnetic potential with noninteger flux. Working with the Friedrichs realization of the magnetic Hamiltonian, we establish global well-posedness for initial data in the weighted magnetic energy space. For mass-critical and mass-supercritical nonlinearities, we prove convergence of the interaction representation in the same weighted space, while in the mass-subcritical range we obtain scattering in the magnetic energy space. The proof is based on a magnetic lens transformation, which converts the original equation into a nonlinear equation governed by the Aharonov--Bohm harmonic oscillator on a finite time interval. Existence is obtained through truncation, compactness, and energy estimates, whereas uniqueness follows directly from the dispersive decay of the confined linear flow. This approach avoids derivative Strichartz estimates, which are delicate in the presence of the singular magnetic field.
comment: 28 pages
☆ Free boundary MHD equilibria with surface tension
Chengchun Hao
Free boundary equilibria of an ideal incompressible magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) plasma, at rest, with surface tension and an exterior vacuum are studied. Within the frozen-in orbit of a reference magnetic field, every equilibrium is a critical point of the magnetic plus surface energy over the space of volume-preserving embeddings; the capillary boundary condition is the first-variation boundary term, and no assumption on the connectivity of the boundary is required. In the plane the frozen-in law fixes the distribution of the stream function and turns the energy into a rearrangement functional. For a single-axis reference field a sharp lower bound is proved that depends only on that distribution and is attained by an explicit area-preserving diffeomorphism, smooth across the axis, which yields a classical equilibrium. For Morse stream functions sharper bounds governed by the level-set topology are obtained, with a strict gap at an isolated simple saddle merge. In three dimensions no such reduction is available: the energy does not control the full gradient of the embedding, no scalar rearrangement principle applies, and the axisymmetric reduction yields only a conditional lower bound.
comment: 41 pages
☆ Dirichlet eigenvalues of Laplacian with potential on general graphs and Weyl limits in integer lattice spaces $Z^d$
Huyuan Chen, Lixun Jia
In this paper, we first establish the existence of weighted Dirichlet eigenvalues of the Laplacian with a vertex weight on an infinite, connected and locally finite graph, via building compact embeddings of suitable spaces, when the weight decays faster at infinity than the optimal Hardy weight. In the particular integer lattice space $Z^d$, we apply a segmentation technique to estimate the mean Riesz potential over the entire space, thereby deriving estimates for the eigenvalue counting function and establishing the Weyl limit of the eigenvalues.
☆ Global solutions of the planar plasma equation with infinite $p$-mass
Daniele Bartolucci, Aleks Javnikar, Juncheng Wei, Ruijun Wu
We study entire solutions of $-Δu=u_+^p$ in the plane for $p>1$. A solution which is nondecreasing in one direction is invariant in that direction, and for each nonconstant solution in this class the plasma region $\{x:u(x)>0\}$ is a strip, the transverse profile has affine tails, and the Morse index is infinite. The stable solutions are the nonpositive constants, and the nonconstant solutions with finite Morse index are precisely the translated and scaled radial profiles of finite $p$-mass, each of which has Morse index one. We also construct a continuous branch of solutions which are periodic in one variable, depend on both variables and have infinite Morse index.
comment: 20 pages. Comments are welcome
☆ The sharp logarithmic loss in vanishing order for real planar Schrödinger equations
Igor Kukavica, Qi Xu
We determine, up to constants, the largest possible order of vanishing of real solutions of $Δu=Vu$ in dimension two in terms of the size of the real potential~$V$. For each sufficiently large integer $k$, we construct a real potential $V\in C_c^\infty(B_1)$ with $\|V\|_\infty$ comparable to $k^2/\log k$ and a smooth real solution $u$ on $\R^2$ that vanishes to order $k$ at the origin, satisfies $\sup_{B_{1/2}}|u|=\|u\|_\infty=1$, and equals a positive constant outside~$B_{7/8}$. Consequently, on every smooth connected closed Riemannian surface, the largest order of vanishing at a prescribed point for real potentials of norm at most $M$ is comparable to $\sqrt{M\log M}$ for large~$M$, uniformly in the point. This gives a negative answer, in dimension two, to the square-root questions of Kukavica and Kenig. With the same building block, we also construct a nonzero real solution on $\R^2$ with $\|V\|_\infty\le1$ and $|u(x)|\le\exp(-c|x|\sqrt{\log|x|})$ for large~$|x|$, so that the Landis conjecture fails in its exponential form in the plane even for real potentials. Both constructions match the estimates of Logunov, Malinnikova, Nadirashvili, and Nazarov, which are therefore sharp.
☆ Critical exponent for Nakao's problem in three space dimensions
Vladimir Georgiev, Kosuke Kita
We study a system consisting of a semilinear damped wave equation coupled to a semilinear wave equation in three space dimensions. We determine the sharp condition on the exponents of nonlinear terms that separates global existence for sufficiently small initial data from finite-time blow-up even for arbitrarily small data satisfying suitable positivity assumptions. To prove global existence, we combine a weighted pointwise estimate for the damped wave equation, which we established in earlier work, with a new one for the wave equation. The new pointwise estimate for the wave equation uses a combination of a parabolic weight and a light-cone weight. For the proof of blow-up, pointwise lower bounds are compared with integral upper bounds obtained by test functions. In the main estimates, explicit physical-space representations reveal how forcing near the wave cone influences the damped component on parabolic spatial scales and, in turn, the wave component inside the cone.
☆ Two 3-Dimensional Coefficient Inverse Problems for Wave-like Equations With a Single Location of the Point Source
Michael V. Klibanov, Jingzhi Li, Tian Niu
In this paper two long standing open questions are addressed for the first time. Those questions are about Lipschitz stability estimates and uniqueness theorems for two Coefficient Inverse Problems (CIPs) for 3-Dimensional wave-like Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) with formally determined input data. We assume that a certain associated PDE is written in finite differences with respect to time t. The unknown coefficients depend on all three spatial variables. The key novelty here is that the input data for these CIPs are generated by only a single location of the point source at the moment of time {t = 0}. In the first CIP (CIP1) the unknown coefficient is the potential of a wave-like PDE. The second CIP (CIP2) is concerned with a far more challenging case when the unknown coefficient is involved in the principal part of the hyperbolic operator. In addition to Lipschitz stability and uniqueness results, numerical methods are developed for both CIPs. Their convergence analysis establishes the global convergence property of both numerical techniques. The latter is unlike the local convergence of conventional numerical procedures for CIPs. The method for CIP1 is tested computationally. Its extensive numerical testing for complicated media structures consistently demonstrates a very accurate performance of this method for noisy input data. The authors declare that artificial intelligence was not used for any part of this work.
comment: 40 pages, 6 figures
☆ A Stackelberg strategy for the semi-linear heat equation with boundary controls
Jose Antoinio Villa
This work continues the results presented in \cite{calsavara2022new} where a hierarchical control problem is solved. Our first goal is the case of both controls acting on the boundary. The follower control solves a null controllability problem, and the leader minimizes a $L^2$ cost functional. Additionally, we solve the case where one control acts on the boundary and the other on an open subset of the domain. More precisely, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a leader-follower couple and give some techniques to solve the problem.
☆ On the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point for the Yamabe equation in all dimensions
Liuwei Gong, YanYan Li, Anthony Matos
We determine the sharp vanishing order of the Weyl tensor at a blow-up point of solutions to the Yamabe equation in every dimension $n\ge 25$. On every closed, connected, smooth $n$-dimensional manifold $M$ of positive Yamabe type and at any prescribed point $p\in M$, we construct a smooth metric $ \widehat g$ and a sequence of smooth positive solutions to the Yamabe equation blowing up at $p$, such that the first nonzero covariant derivative of the Weyl tensor at $p$ has any prescribed order $l$ satisfying $l\ge 6$ when $25\le n\le 29$, $l \ge 4$ when $30\le n\le 51$, and $l\ge 2$ when $n\ge 52$. Moreover, $|\nabla_{ \widehat g}^{l}W_{ \widehat g}|>0$ everywhere on $M$. Earlier constructions realize every strictly higher order as the first nonzero order, while the known Weyl vanishing results exclude every lower first nonzero order. Thus the endpoint cases $l=6,4,2$ were the only ones left open, and are settled here. In particular, the order-two examples show that the compactness criterion $|W|+|\nabla W|>0$ is sharp. At the endpoints, the construction arranges global and localized metric perturbations to interact at leading order in a limiting functional. For $l=2,4$, anisotropic polynomial ansatzes involving two orthogonal algebraic Weyl tensors remove a distinguished translation degeneracy and produce $C^1$-stable saddle points. For $l=6$, a different polynomial ansatz produces a nondegenerate local minimum. Higher prescribed orders are obtained by separating the perturbation that determines the limiting functional from the one that prescribes the Weyl derivative.
☆ Spectral bounds of cooperative nonlocal dispersal systems: monotonicity, domain limits, and applications
Mingxin Wang, Lei Zhang
We study the spectral bound of cooperative nonlocal dispersal systems on bounded domains. The spectral bound is continuous under uniform coefficient and suitable nested domain perturbations, and strictly monotone with respect to the coefficients and the domain if either corresponding operator admits a principal eigenvalue. Further results include small-domain limits, large-domain limits for even convolution kernels under suitable coefficient assumptions, and criteria for a unique critical domain size. Applications yield a unique extinction-persistence threshold in the interval length for a heterogeneous epidemic model and a sharp spreading-vanishing threshold for a scalar free-boundary problem. These thresholds remain valid when the spectral bound vanishes on an interval, with the critical habitat length given by its right endpoint.
☆ Controlability of the 1D wave equation by point sources: outgoing states, circle rotations and small divisors
Kaïs Ammari, Mourad Sini
We characterise the states reachable from rest for the one-dimensional wave equation on the real line driven by finitely many fixed point sources. The characterisation reduces the control problem to a cohomological equation on a circle whose length is twice the distance between the outermost sources, with support constraints determined by the control time. For two sources, the reachable set is closed and the controls are unique at every finite time. For three sources, we give a complete classification in terms of the control time and the ratio of the two relevant travel times. Below the time needed to traverse the outer interval twice, reachability is described by finite orbit sums. At and above this threshold, an irrational ratio produces a dense, non-closed reachable set in the compatible outgoing-state space, and exact reachability is determined by a small-divisor condition. We also quantify the cost of control. The minimum control norm is equivalent to the energy norm of the target plus a weighted Fourier norm of its periodised defect. For a badly approximable irrational ratio, the worst cost for defects of Fourier degree at most $N$ grows linearly in $N$, i.e. Liouville ratios produce superpolynomial growth along subsequences. We derive constructive approximation estimates and sharp worst-case cost--accuracy rates on Sobolev classes of defects. For an arbitrary number of sources, the long-time classification and the quantitative estimates are governed by simultaneous Diophantine approximation of the source positions.
☆ The Kalton--Peck space disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture
Veli Shakhmurov, Rishad Shahmurov
We prove that the classical complex Kalton--Peck space $Z_2$ is not isomorphic to $[X,H]_θ$ for any UMD Banach space $X$, Hilbert space $H$, and $0<θ<1$. Since $Z_2$ is UMD, this disproves Rubio de Francia's conjecture on intermediate UMD spaces. The proof combines the logarithmic block identity, a shift-commutator estimate on the interpolation strip, a unified obstruction in terms of reciprocal Hilbert norms, and Hahn--Banach with elementary convexity. It allows arbitrary compatible placements. We also realize $Z_2$ as a quotient of a closed subspace of an intermediate UMD space for every fixed interpolation parameter less than one.
♻ ☆ Construction of two-bubble solutions for the energy-critical Hartree equation
Jacek Jendrej, Xuemei Li, Guixiang Xu
We construct a pure two-bubble solution for the focusing, energy-critical Hartree equation in space dimension $N \geq 7$. The constructed solution is spherically symmetric, global in (at least) the negative time direction and asymptotically behaves as a superposition of two ground states (or bubbles) both centered at the origin, with the ratio of their length scales converging to $0$ and the phases of the two bubbles form the right angle. The main arguments are the modulation analysis, the bootstrap argument and the topological argument. The main novelty with respect to existing constructions of pure two-bubble solutions is the nonlocal interaction, which is more complex to analyze.

♻ ☆ Smooth local isometric embeddings in dimension four
Zhouyu Long
Every smooth four-dimensional Riemannian metric admits a local isometric embedding into $\mathbb{R}^{10}$, the optimal universal dimension. A fixed-domain Nash-Moser argument prescribes any Gauss-compatible rank-six second fundamental form with regular characteristic data. For $n\ge4$, product-weighted cube evaluations give polynomial Gram lifts of algebraic curvature tensors that are uniformly positive on a fixed $n(n-1)/2$-dimensional support. In dimension four the support can have a nonsingular complex characteristic quartic. With linear tangential control, the transverse square-root estimate near affine embeddings is sharp in $H^\ell$ for $\ell\ge1$.

♻ ☆ Nondegeneracy of low-energy nodal solutions to the Yamabe equation
Sérgio L. N. Neves, Angela Pistoia
We study the linearized Yamabe equation in $\R^n$, or equivalently on $\s^n$, at a low-energy sign-changing solution with two nodal domains. We consider odd dimensions $n=2k-1$ and a solution invariant under $Γ=O(k)\times O(k)$. Its regular level sets are isoparametric hypersurfaces, which foliate the sphere away from the two focal submanifolds. This symmetry reduces the equation for the solution to a singular ODE. In the balanced case, we choose a single-node profile that is odd under reflection across the midpoint. We prove nondegeneracy in the $Γ$-invariant subspace for every $k\ge2$, and in the full space $H^1(\s^n)$ for sufficiently large $k$: every kernel element is generated by a conformal invariance of the equation. The proof uses separation of variables, Wronskian identities and comparison functions adapted to the singular equations for the angular modes.
♻ ☆ Continuity equation on metric spaces via measure-valued derivations and BV-Wasserstein curves
Ehsan Abedi, Zhenhao Li, Timo Schultz
We introduce a notion of continuity equation on metric spaces that is capable of describing curves of probability measures which are absolutely continuous or, more generally, of bounded variation (BV) with respect to the 1-Wasserstein distance. This continuity equation is based on a notion of measure-valued derivations, whose basic theory is also developed in this paper. On $\mathbb{R}^n$, our formulation is consistent with the continuity equation with singular flux introduced by Almi--Rossi--Savaré (arXiv:2506.15333), including the corresponding notion of minimal solutions when the norm is strictly convex. In this work, we characterize BV-curves in the space of probability measures equipped with the (extended) 1-Wasserstein distance as those curves satisfying the continuity equation with a measure-valued derivation of finite mass. To this aim, we extend our previous work (Calc. Var. (2024) 63:16) on probabilistic representations on BV-curves and construct from them measure-valued derivations (resp. flux measures) on geodesic metric spaces (resp. on $\mathbb{R}^n$).

♻ ☆ The polygonal Weinstock inequality and quantitative stability
Zhuo Cheng, Yian Zhang
For every integer $N \ge 3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes the perimeter-normalized first positive Steklov eigenvalue $J(P) = |\partial P|σ_1(P)$ among all simple planar polygons $P$ with at most $N$ sides, up to similarity. More generally, if $P$ has $p$ strictly convex vertices and $q$ reflex vertices after merging consecutive collinear sides, then $J(P) \le J(R_{p+\min(q,2)})$, with equality if and only if $q = 0$ and $P$ is similar to $R_p$. Among polygons with at most $N$ sides, restricting to those that are nonconvex or have fewer than $N$ genuine sides lowers the supremum of $J$ by $12πζ(3)N^{-4} + O(N^{-5})$ as $N \to \infty$, with a positive gap for every $N \ge 4$. For convex $p$-gons, the spectral deficit $J(R_p) - J(P)$ controls the normalized squared deviations of support heights, midpoint offsets, and side lengths with weights $1$, $p^{-2}$, and $p^{-3}$, as well as $p^{-3}$ times the sum of squared exterior-angle deviations from $2π/p$; the length weight $p^{-3}$ is sharp. For triangles, the deficit is instead comparable to the square root of the relative area deficit at fixed perimeter, or equivalently to $1 - r$, where $r$ is the singular-value ratio of an affine map from an equilateral triangle. Independently of the number of reflex vertices, a boundary phase identity in arc-length balanced disk coordinates yields the sharp fourth-order bound $2π/J(P) - 1 \ge 2ζ(3)p^{-3} + 8ζ(4)p^{-4} + O(p^{-5})$. For fixed $p$, a degree-$p$ Blaschke transport links this identity to $H^{1/p}$ coercivity for the regularized square root of the conformal derivative, perimeter-concentration rigidity at equally spaced convex prevertices, and quadratic Hausdorff stability for $p \ge 4$.

♻ ☆ Separation points and pressure gradients for the nonstationary Stokes system with localized boundary data in the half-space
Kyungkeun Kang, Chanhong Min
We study separation points of the nonstationary Stokes system in a half-space with zero initial data and nonnegative, space-time separable boundary data supported in the unit ball and in $[0,1]$, respectively. A separation point is a pair $(x',t)$, with $x'$ outside the spatial support, arbitrarily near which a velocity component takes both signs. The main ingredient is an explicit representation of the velocity and pressure via confluent hypergeometric functions. For normal boundary data, if the temporal boundary data are regular and unimodal, log-concavity yields a unique separation time for the $i$th tangential component at every boundary point with $|x_i|>1$, and exactly two for the normal component at distant points, one before and one after the boundary data vanish. The later one, a simple zero of the second normal derivative of the normal component at the boundary, is unique even without unimodality. We obtain monotonicity and asymptotics of separation times and vanishing rates of normal derivatives. For tangential boundary data with $n\geq3$, under the same assumptions, a separation time for the velocity component in their direction exists at $x'$ with $|x'|>1$ precisely when the corresponding Riesz transform of the spatial boundary data has a positive derivative in that direction at $x'$, and log-concavity makes it unique. For the remaining components, we prove existence and uniqueness of separation points on distant lines parallel to the axes, with asymptotics in terms of spatial moments and support geometry. For radial spatial boundary data, we determine the signs and zero sets of tangential pressure derivatives.

♻ ☆ 1-Laplacian type problems with strongly singular nonlinearities and gradient terms
Daniela Giachetti, Francescantonio Oliva, Francesco Petitta
We show optimal existence, nonexistence and regularity results for nonnegative solutions to Dirichlet problems as $$ \begin{cases} \displaystyle -Δ_1 u = g(u)|D u|+h(u)f & \text{in}\;Ω,\\ u=0 & \text{on}\;\partialΩ, \end{cases} $$ where $Ω$ is an open bounded subset of $\mathbb{R}^N$, $f\geq 0$ belongs to $L^N(Ω)$, and $g$ and $h$ are continuous functions that may blow up at zero. As a noteworthy fact we show how a non-trivial interaction mechanism between the two nonlinearities $g$ and $h$ produces remarkable regularizing effects on the solutions. The sharpness of our main results is discussed through the use of appropriate explicit examples.
♻ ☆ Stability of 3D Stratified Plane Couette Flow: A New Lift-up Mechanism and Potential Vorticity
Yiting Yao
Since the pioneering work of Taylor and Goldstein in 1931 laid the foundation for the study of parallel stratified shear flows, non-parallel configurations have received comparatively little attention. We study the stability of the 3D Boussinesq system near the plane Couette flow $V^*=(y,0,0)$ under the vertically stratified background $η^*=αz$. The shear and stratification directions are perpendicular. This geometry produces two structural effects that are absent in the parallel configuration: an additional nonlocal coupling in the non-zero-mode system, which obstructs a directly useful symmetrization, and a wave-shear coupled lift-up mechanism for the zero modes. The transient growth due to the lift-up effect can be suppressed either by sufficiently strong stratification or under suitable assumptions on the initial data. To study the nonzero-mode system, we introduce a reformulation based on the linearized potential vorticity (PV), a fundamental quantity in geophysical fluid dynamics, to recover a better energy structure. We establish the inviscid damping of $u_{1,\neq}$ and $u_{2,\neq}$. We further apply the linearized PV formulation to study the linear stability of the tilted Couette flow. Finally, we use this formulation to prove the nonlinear stability for perturbations on $\mathbb{T}\times\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{T}$ and show that strong stratification can enhance the stability.
comment: Rewrote Section 2.2 and improved Lemma 2.4. Revised the Introduction and split the nonlinear stability theorem into two parts
♻ ☆ Invariant subspaces and nest algebras in left-right operator splitting
Mark Spivack
The left--right (L-R) splitting method for boundary integral equations in rough-surface scattering writes the integral operator as the sum of its lower- and strictly upper- triangular parts. This note examines the operator algebra formed by the lower-triangular ($L$-type) parts.Their weak closure is a nest algebra; second-kind $L$-type operators with Hilbert--Schmidt kernels have $L$-type inverses; and Arveson's distance formula expresses the error of the best possible forward-only approximation in terms of the backward coupling across a single cut. Bounds and numerical results for the 2D double-layer kernel suggest that truncation is close to optimal, and that the worst-case input field is a predominantly left-going grazing wave rather than backscatter of a right-going incident field. For a hard surface the inverse $L$-operator is given, up to a second-order correction, by four times the $L$-operator of the mirror-image surface, and several open questions are posed.

♻ ☆ Orbital Stability of Smooth Traveling Solitary Waves to the Fornberg-Whitham Equation
Xijun Deng, Stephane Lafortune, Zhisu Liu
The Fornberg-Whitham (FW) equation was introduced by Fornberg and Whitham [Fornberg and Whitham, Phil. Trans. R. Soc. Lond. A (1978)] as a nonlocal model for unidirectional shallow water waves capable of capturing wave steepening and breaking. Despite its similarities with integrable shallow-water equations, the FW equation is not completely integrable. Nevertheless, the FW equation is part of the family of peakon-type models as it supports peaked traveling wave solutions. In this paper, we consider smooth solitary wave solutions to the FW equation. We use a variational approach to show that some are orbitally stable.

For hyperbolic systems of conservation laws (without any genuine nonlinearity of linear degeneracy assumption on the flux) we construct a quadratic interaction functional, which controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions and it is local in time. ♻ ☆ A local-in-time quadratic functional for scalar conservation laws
Egor Baitenov, Stefano Modena
We construct a Glimm-type functional for scalar conservation laws, which is quadratic (w.r.t. the total variation of the initial datum), it controls the change of wavefront speed across interactions, and, differently than functionals with similar properties already present in the literature, it is purely local in time, meaning that it depends only on the present profile of the (approximate) solution (and not on its past or future evolution).

♻ ☆ Relaxation to hydrostatic equilibria for two-dimensional inhomogeneous incompressible viscous flows under a conservative force
Song Jiang, Quan Wang
This paper studies the two-dimensional inhomogeneous Navier--Stokes equations governing stratified flows in a bounded domain under a gravitational potential \(f\). Our main results are as follows. First, we provide a rigorous characterization of steady states, proving that under the Dirichlet condition \(\mathbf{u}|_{\partial Ω} = \mathbf{0}\), all admissible equilibria are hydrostatic and satisfy \(\nabla p_s = -ρ_s \nabla f\). Second, through a perturbative analysis around arbitrary hydrostatic profiles, we show that despite possible transient growth induced by the Rayleigh--Taylor mechanism, the system always relaxes to a hydrostatic equilibrium. Third, we identify a necessary and sufficient condition on the initial density perturbation for convergence to a linear hydrostatic density profile of the form \(ρ_s = -γf + β\), with \(γ> 0\) and \(β> 0\). Finally, we establish improved regularity estimates for strong solutions corresponding to initial data in the Sobolev space \(H^3(Ω)\).
♻ ☆ Notes for a seminar on vortex layer cascades
Andrés Laín-Sanclemente
After the seminars I recently gave at New York University, the University of Chicago, Princeton University and the University of Bonn and after having been asked by some people to publish these notes, I decided to upload them to arXiv. In recent years, the method of vortex layer cascades has successfully been applied to construct finite-time singularities in multiple fluid equations (3D Euler, Boussinesq, IPM, g-SQG...). In this talk, I will motivate and describe the method and sketch how it can be applied to the 2D Boussinesq and 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations. In both systems, the growth of the vorticity is driven by an accumulated hysteresis effect triggered by the cyclic deformation of the density layers, whose dynamics is governed by an infinite chain of degenerate pendula. Our work also settles the previously open question about global existence of classical solutions of the (forced) 2D non-homogeneous Euler equations.

☆ A Rellich-type inequality for the sphere

We prove a Rellich-type inequality of the form $$\int |(Δ+ 1)u|^2dx \geq C_d \int \frac{|u|^2}{(1 - |x|^2)^2}dx $$ for smooth functions $u$ compactly supported in the unit ball in $\mathbb{R}^d$ for $d \geq 1$. The obtained constant is asymptotically sharp up to the first three orders, as $d \rightarrow \infty$. We also show that in the complement of the ball, the inequality holds only in dimension one, and does not hold true with a positive $C_d>0$ for $d \geq 2$. The motivation is that if $\hat{u}$ denotes the Fourier transform of $u$, then the inequality is associated with the uncertainty principle $$ \left(\int |u|^2dx\right)^2 \lesssim \int (1-|x|^2)^2|u|^2dx \int (1 - |ξ|^2)^2|\hat{u}|^2 dξ,$$ which says that a function cannot be simultaneously concentrated on a sphere in both space and frequency. This is in analogy with the classical Hardy inequality together with the Heisenberg uncertainty principle.

We develop a linearization theory for completely Lipschitz mappings between operator spaces. Motivated by the classical theory of Lipschitz-free spaces, we introduce a completely Lipschitz-free space and show that completely Lipschitz mappings admit a canonical linearization as completely bounded operators on this space. We provide several equivalent descriptions of this operator space, extending to the noncommutative setting the classical constructions of Arens--Eells, de Leeuw, and Dixmier--Ng. In particular, we obtain a molecular description, a quotient representation of an operator $\ell_1$-space, and a realization as the closed linear span of evaluation functionals. Our framework applies over both the real and complex scalar fields; in the real case, we first establish some operator space results needed to carry out the constructions. We also show that our notion of completely Lipschitz mapping encompasses the previously introduced extensions of Lipschitz mappings to operator spaces. These results provide a unified framework for studying Lipschitz phenomena in the setting of operator spaces and establish the corresponding free operator spaces as a natural tool for their linearization.

This answers a question by Shimorin, and greatly extends his result that any space of Dirichlet type is CNP. As a byproduct of our investigation, we also show that if the forward shift on $\mathcal{H}$ is concave, then any multiplier of $\mathcal{H}$ is the SOT limit of its Cesàro means. Can a group be colored red and blue, with both color classes infinite, so that each right translation changes the color of only finitely many elements? For the group of finite subsets of the natural numbers, one can color a nonempty set by the parity of its largest element (and the empty set red). Holt proved that no such coloring exists in an uncountable locally finite group. For the finitary coarse structure, right almost invariant subsets are exactly the coarsely clopen sets; modulo finite changes, their characteristic functions give all the projections in the Higson corona algebra. We give a detailed, self-contained account of Holt's coset argument in Cornulier's formulation, without using group cohomology. The argument shows why the space of coarse ends is a singleton and the full Higson corona is connected. We then give a proof of Protasov's stronger conclusion for any uncountable abelian group---in particular, an uncountable direct sum of groups of order two---showing that the full Higson corona is a singleton.

Without noise, no such bound can hold, since the conductive state is a solution with $Nu=1$ for every Rayleigh number. The proof uses the auxiliary functional method. For general Markov processes, we show that the defining inequality of an auxiliary functional need only hold after a short time average. This reduces the problem to showing that, with uniformly positive probability, the solution quickly leaves the set of states with low heat flux and low thermal dissipation. We establish this by projecting onto an unstable eigenvector of the linearization around the initial mean temperature profile, yielding a one-dimensional Itô process with linear growth, additive noise, and nonlinear error terms.

Hence the lifting needs no hypothesis for Riemann data, and for Cauchy data it survives exactly on an integral curve of an eigenvector field, where we give an implicit solution; off that curve the state path leaves it at a rate we compute. We then ask when an implicit closed-form solution exists for arbitrary data. For homogeneous quadratic fluxes these are precisely the systems linearly equivalent to two decoupled Burgers equations (the curve $a=1+b^2$ of the Schaeffer--Shearer normal form). Every such system loses strict hyperbolicity along a full line, so no model with an isolated umbilic point qualifies, among them the quadratic Corey model of three-phase flow. In this paper, we rigorously derive this formula from a variational principle based on Arnold's energy--Casimir method, without prescribing any of these geometric or physical quantities a priori. We introduce a scale-invariant variational principle involving the energy, impulse, and $L^p$ Casimir invariants. For $1 < p < \infty$, we construct orbitally stable energy-maximizing vortex rings and investigate how their geometry depends on the Casimir exponent $p$. In contrast, as $p\to1^+$, the energy-maximizing vortex rings concentrate onto a circular filament of radius $e^{1/3}$, uniquely selected by the variational principle. After suitable translations and rescalings, their vortex-core profiles converge to an optimizer of the logarithmic Hardy--Littlewood--Sobolev inequality. Introducing an effective core radius $ε_p$ determined by the entropy of the vorticity distribution, we establish the Kelvin--Hicks formula \begin{align*} W_p = \frac{Γ_p}{4πR_p} \left(\log\frac{8R_p}{ε_p}-1+o(1)\right) \quad \textrm{as}\ p\to1^+, \end{align*} where $W_p$, $Γ_p$, and $R_p$ denote the propagation speed, circulation, and effective ring radius, respectively. In particular, the constant correction $-1$ is obtained for nonuniform vortex-core profiles without imposing any prescribed core structure.

♻ ☆ Direct Scattering of the Focusing Nonlinear Schrödinger Equation with Step-like Oscillatory Initial Data
Tamara Grava, Robert Jenkins, Xiaofan Zhang, Zechuan Zhang
In this manuscript we set up the direct and inverse scattering problems for step-like traveling wave solutions of the nonlinear Schrödinger equation. Specifically, we consider the initial data $u_0(x)=u_e^\ell(x)$ for $x<0$ and $u_0(x)=u_e^r(x)$ for $x>0$, where $u_e^\ell(x)$ and $u_e^r(x)$ are elliptic traveling wave solutions of NLS. More generally, we consider initial data satisfying $u_0(x)\to u_e^\ell(x)$ as $x\to-\infty$ and $u_0(x)\to u_e^r(x)$ as $x\to+\infty$. Under the assumption that $u_0-u_e^\ell \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^-)$ and $u_0-u_e^r \in L^{1,2}(\mathbb{R}^+)$, we formulate the direct scattering problem and establish analytic properties of the scattering data. We then formulate the inverse problem as a Riemann--Hilbert problem and prove its solvability, thus proving the existence of the nonlinear Schrödinger solution with the above step-like initial data. Finally, we observe that our Riemann--Hilbert formulation is a special case of the one arising for full soliton-gas initial data.

♻ ☆ Discrete unique continuation for Schrödinger equations
Torunn S. Jensen, Didier Pilod, João P. G. Ramos
We study discrete unique continuation for one-dimensional Schrödinger equations. We prove that if a solution vanishes at the points $\pm n^α$ at time $0$ and at the points $\pm n^β$ at time $1$, it must vanish identically in two main cases: the case of a Schrödinger equation with a real potential that is uniformly of Gevrey class $σ\ge 0$ in space, provided that $\max\{1,σ\}\big(α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)\big)<1$, and in the case of the cubic nonlinear Schrödinger equation, provided that $α/(1-α)+β/(1-β)<1$. Unlike previous results for logarithmically spaced zeros, our methods do not rely on complex analysis. We first show that, whenever $α+β<1$, the zeros force the solution to lie in the Schwartz class at all times. We then convert the zeros into gaussian decay at the two times, by combining energy estimates for iterations of the vector field $Γ=x+2it\partial_x$ with techniques from Fourier uniqueness problems, and conclude with the Morgan-type uncertainty principle of Escauriaza, Kenig, Ponce and Vega.

♻ ☆ A Unified Heat-Ball Framework for Fokker--Planck Equations: Mean-Value Identities, Exact Sampling, and Error Analysis
Jiayao Bai, Yi Du, Rongxing Lai, Yifei Jia
Diffusion-based generative models with nonlinear or learned forward drifts raise questions that stay hidden for Gaussian forward processes: how the divergence-free and gradient parts of the drift shape the evolving density, whether sampling can draw on local rather than global information, and how to treat low-density regions, where $u$ carries a weak signal while $\log u$ diverges and the entropy density $u\log u$ falls between the two. These questions motivate the present study of local representations for Fokker--Planck equations with general, possibly nonlinear and time-dependent drift. We derive inhomogeneous heat-ball identities for the density $u$, the log-density $\log u$, the entropy density $u\log u$, and the score $\nabla\log u$, keeping the source terms generated by the drift; their unscaled residuals recover the corresponding differential residuals at leading order in the squared heat-ball radius. The weights appearing in the identities, the source integrals, and the integration-by-parts formulas all belong to a single Beta--Gamma family of measures on the heat ball, which gives exact rejection-free sampling, product quadrature, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimators with variance and cost bounds that are explicit in the dimension and the radius. Experiments with Gaussian-mixture and nonlinear-drift references, in dimensions up to $1024$ where applicable, confirm the sampling laws, the identities, and the residual behavior. In particular, log-density and score evaluations remain accurate where direct density estimation breaks down, and the heat-ball residuals provide local consistency tests for learned score models. A study of gauge-based heat-ball walks illustrates a recursive use of the density identity.

♻ ☆ Transmission and Reflection coefficients for Schrödinger Operators with Truncated Periodic Potentials that support defect states
Joseph C. Stellman, Jeremy L. Marzuola
We consider scattering waves through truncated periodic potentials with perturbations that support localized gap eigenstates. In a small complex neighborhood around an assumed positive bound state of the model operator, we prove the existence of a distinct zero reflection state, or transmission resonance. We compare its location to a previously found scattering resonance and use the properties of solutions near these interesting points to analyze the behavior of transmission and reflection coefficients of scattering solutions near the assumed bound state. By example, we also discuss the truncated simple harmonic oscillator and compare the analysis to the crystalline case.

♻ ☆ Isolated yet highly unstable 2D Euler equilibria
Alberto Enciso, Antonio J. Fernández, Marc Nualart
We construct steady solutions of the two-dimensional Euler equations on smooth annular domains that are isolated, modulo scaling, in the $L^\infty$ vorticity topology. They are highly unstable: any Yudovich trajectory remaining sufficiently close to such an equilibrium on an open time interval is a stationary multiple of it, they admit wandering neighborhoods of initial data for all non-zero time and, moreover, at fixed energy, enstrophy and circulations, distinct nearby trajectories cannot return even weakly to the equilibrium. Further, on any non-circular annular domain, we show that this kind of isolated, highly unstable equilibria occurs arbitrarily close in the Yudovich norm to smooth equilibria which are themselves non-isolated.

♻ ☆ Edge State Propagation Near Multiple and Singular Interfaces
Nicolas Frantz, {É}ric Vacelet
We study the semiclassical propagation of edge-states for a two-dimensional Dirac operator with a spatially varying mass. The zero set of the mass models the interface between topological phases and is allowed either to consist of two disjoint smooth curves or to possess an isolated singular point. For disjoint interfaces, we prove that a wave packet initially localized on one component remains confined near this interface over long semiclassical time scales and we quantify the influence of the distance between the two components on the accuracy of the approximation. For singular interfaces, we determine the regime in which the wave-packet approximation remains valid as the packet approaches the singularity and identify the scaling at which our estimates lose their uniformity.
♻ ☆ Endowing phase-field fracture models with custom strength criteria
Roberto Alessi, Matteo Brunetti, Roshan Udaram Patil, Jacinto Ulloa
By now, several approaches have been proposed to endow phase-field fracture models with the ability to describe crack nucleation under multiaxial stress states. These include techniques for splitting the free energy, direct modifications of the phase-field driving or resisting forces, and the introduction of additional internal variables, such as plastic strains or other nonlinear strains. In this paper, we propose a fundamentally different strategy for incorporating arbitrary elastic domains into phase-field fracture models, formulated within the energetic framework of generalized standard materials. The proposed approach relies on letting the dissipation potential depend on the current state of the material. In this way, the elastic degradation and the strength criterion remain two distinct and independently controllable aspects of the material response, while the governing equations directly descend from a local stability condition and energy balance. Simple yet representative models are presented and thoroughly discussed to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methodology. The resulting evolution of the elastic domain is investigated in both strain and stress spaces under proportional and non-proportional loading paths, with the latter highlighting the path dependence of the dissipated work. Moreover, numerical simulations demonstrate a range of crack nucleation processes under multiaxial loading conditions for various analytical strength surfaces. The present work paves the way for future developments and applications in several directions, including crack propagation studies and dedicated numerical solution strategies.
♻ ☆ A posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems
Andreas Dedner, Jan Giesselmann, Kiwoong Kwon, Tristan Pryer
This work provides reliable a posteriori error estimates for Runge-Kutta discontinuous Galerkin approximations of nonlinear convection-diffusion systems. The classes of systems we study are quite general, with a focus on convection-dominated problems and systems with partial diffusion. Our a posteriori error bounds are valid for a family of discontinuous Galerkin spatial discretizations and various temporal discretizations that include explicit and implicit-explicit time-stepping schemes, popular tools for practical simulations of this class of problem. We prove that our estimators provide reliable upper bounds for the error of the numerical method and present numerical evidence showing that, in the convection-dominated regime, the residual quantities converge at the same rates as the discretization errors. Since one of our main interests is the convection dominant case, we also track the dependence of the estimator on the viscosity coefficient.

♻ ☆ Quantitative homogenization for the critical long-range random conductance model
Ahmed Bou-Rabee, Paul Dario
We consider the long-range random conductance model on $\mathbb{Z}^d$ at the critical exponent: the jump rate between sites $x$ and $y$ is $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\}) |x-y|^{-(d+2)}$, where the conductances $\mathbf{a}(\{x,y\})$ are independent, uniformly elliptic and have a common mean. Below the critical exponent $(d+2)$ the walk converges to a stable process; above it, to Brownian motion with diffusive $\sqrt{t}$ scaling. At criticality the second moment of the jump kernel diverges logarithmically. We establish quantitative homogenization of the associated heat equation at the rate $1/\sqrt{|\ln \varepsilon|}$. As a consequence, we deduce annealed convergence of the random walk to Brownian motion under the anomalous $\sqrt{t \log t}$ scaling. Unlike in standard homogenization, the effective diffusivity is determined by the mean conductance alone, with no corrector contribution at leading order.

♻ ☆ Velocity Averaging for the Wigner Equation with Electromagnetic Fields
François Golse, Jakob Möller
We discuss the application of $L^2$-based velocity averaging to the Wigner kinetic equation governing the quantum evolution of the Wigner transform of a density operator of a particle subjected to an external electromagnetic field. This extends the $L^2$-based averaging lemma from [F. Golse, J. Möller: Commun. Math. Sci. (2026)] to electromagnetic fields. We make use of the magnetic or gauge-invariant Wigner transform due to Stratonovich [Sov. Phys. Dokl., 1:414-418, 1956] which differs from the usual definition by a phase factor involving the circulation of the magnetic vector potential along a line segment. The magnetic Wigner transform obeys the Wigner equation in the generalized phase space variables $(x,v=ξ-A(t,x))$, which is a more natural setting for the application of velocity averaging. Since the magnetic Wigner equation contains a first order derivative in the spatial variable, we obtain compactness in $L^2_{\mathrm{loc}}$ but no gain in regularity.

♻ ☆ Well-posedness and finite-time breakdown for Euler-alignment systems with diffusive chemotaxis
Marta Menci, Marco Papi
We investigate a recent class of pressureless Euler systems arising in biological contexts, in which the velocity evolution is driven, besides the nonlocal alignment interaction, by the gradient of a concentration self-produced by the population. We first establish local existence and uniqueness of strong solutions, in a class requiring no spatial derivative of the initial population density, together with a continuation criterion. We then derive sufficient conditions on the initial data for finite-time breakdown in the multidimensional setting, with an explicit upper bound for the maximal time of existence. Numerical simulations complement the analysis and illustrate the transition between regular and singular regimes, and the role of the chemotactic strength in the onset of blow-up.
♻ ☆ Global mild solutions and the semiclassical limit for the Fermi--Dirac BGK model
Young-Pil Choi, Byung-Hoon Hwang, Sihyun Song
We prove global existence of mild solutions to the spatially inhomogeneous Fermi--Dirac BGK equation for arbitrary-size Pauli-admissible initial data with finite mass and kinetic energy, allowing both vacuum and locally saturated zero-temperature states. The construction relies on a moment-compatible regularization of the local equilibrium that preserves the Pauli bound and uniform moment control while remaining consistent up to the saturation boundary. The solutions satisfy mass, momentum, and energy conservation and, under an additional finite spatial second-moment assumption, an entropy-gap H-theorem on the full Pauli interval. Under uniform moment and entropy bounds, we further prove that, after extraction of a subsequence, quantum mild solutions converge strongly in phase space, uniformly on bounded time intervals, to a mild solution of the classical BGK equation.

♻ ☆ Sharp double logarithmic Brezis-Gallouët-Wainger inequalities in dimension four
Mohamed Majdoub, Tarek Saanouni
The space $H^2(\mathbb{R}^4)$ is not contained in $L^\infty(\mathbb{R}^4)$. For functions in $H^2_0$ of the unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^4$ that are also Hölder continuous of order $α$, the supremum norm can nevertheless be controlled by the $L^2$ norm of the Laplacian, at the cost of a logarithm of the Hölder seminorm. We determine the optimal leading constant in this estimate. With a double logarithmic correction, the optimal constant is $1/(8π^2α)$. With a single logarithm, the estimate holds for every larger constant and fails for $1/(8π^2α)$ itself. No symmetry assumption is made. The proof reduces the question to a biharmonic obstacle problem with an obstacle of Hölder type. Its minimizer is radial and explicit, and the sharp constant is determined by the asymptotic behaviour of the free boundary radius. We also derive versions of these inequalities on balls and on the whole space. The results are second-order analogues in dimension four of the two-dimensional inequalities of Ibrahim, Majdoub and Masmoudi.

♻ ☆ A Pogorelov-type estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampère equation

We establish a Pogorelov type interior $C^2$ estimate for the real twisted Monge-Ampere equation without assuming uniform ellipticity. This equation is fully nonlinear and elliptic, but is neither concave nor a function of the eigenvalues of the Hessian, so the standard techniques for interior second-derivative estimates do not directly apply. Building on the partial Legendre transform formulation of Streets and Warren, we derive a differential identity for the associated positive-definite matrix $W(D^2u)$ and use some linear algebra to control the third-order terms arising in the maximum principle argument. As an application, we prove a Liouville theorem for entire split convex solutions with quadratic growth, extending the rigidity theorem of Streets and Warren by replacing their uniform ellipticity hypothesis with suitable quadratic growth assumptions.
