♻ ☆ The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
Cong Chen, Yong Li
We consider one-dimensional discrete Schrödinger operators with a periodic background and independent Bernoulli disorder. We ask for the least background period permitting infinitely many gaps in the almost sure spectrum. We provide explicit rational parameters at the minimum period of three, answering Wood's question. Our example gives negative answers to Bellissard's question for a disconnected background hull and to Damanik and Fillman's two finite-gap questions for transitive subshifts of finite type and subshifts of positive entropy. The proof, which appears to be new, normalizes the first background value to zero and establishes a transverse heteroclinic connection at nonzero energy. A strict scale window yields invariant multicones. For every nondegenerate Bernoulli law, gaps accumulate from the right at this spectral point. This accumulation persists under small perturbations, with its energy varying real analytically. Spectral intervals approach this point from the right, ruling out a Cantor spectrum. Three is the least background period at which exact recovery of the spectrum from periodic realizations can require unbounded fundamental periods of the total potential.
♻ ☆ Large-time behavior and accuracy of the Mean-Field Ensemble Kalman Filter in the Linear Detectable Setting
Franca Hoffmann, Sangmin Park, Andrew M. Stuart
The ensemble Kalman filter (EnKF), originally developed in the geophysical sciences, is now widely used for state and parameter estimation problems in various domains of application, and in particular in high dimensional settings. It may be viewed as a robust, cheap-to-implement,alternative to the optimal, Bayesian, filter. However, despite its empirical successes, theoretical understanding of its properties, in relation to the optimal filter, is in its infancy. We contribute novel theoretical understanding, studying the behavior of the EnKF in the infinite particle number setting; this is known as the mean-field ensemble Kalman filter (MFEnKF). In the linear setting with Gaussian noise and Gaussian initial data the MFEnKF coincides with the optimal filter, which is characterized by the Kalman filter. Our focus in this paper will be the linear setting with Gaussian noise, but with non-Gaussian initial data. Under the assumptions of nondegeneracy of the signal noise and detectability of the signal-observation pair we make three specific contributions, studying both discrete and continuous formulations of the methodology. First, in discrete time, we derive the MFEnKF via a variational approximation of the Bayes update using a covariance-weighted optimal transport metric. Secondly, we use this metric to show that the MFEnKF is a strict contraction towards the subspace of Gaussian measures, giving explicit geometric rates in terms of the covariances, in both discrete and continuous time. Finally, in the continuous-time setting, we deduce a stable form of almost sure accuracy of the MFEnKF: given any pair of initial laws (satisfying mild conditions) for the MFEnKF and the optimal filter, the 2-Wasserstein distance between their distributions decays exponentially, for almost every observation path.

♻ ☆ An Orlicz variational formula for David-type Beltrami equations
Ryo Matsuda
We develop a Banach-space variational theory for degenerate Beltrami equations of David type. For coefficients supported in a bounded domain $\mathcal{U}\subset\mathbb{C}$, the pointwise change of variables $ν=2μ/(1-|μ|^2)$ identifies the David coefficients with the exponential Orlicz space $L^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ for $Φ(s)=e^s-s-1$. On the open subset of parameters with a sufficiently large exponential moment, the principal solution map is locally real $C^{1,1}$ into $W^{1,2}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\mathbb{C})$, with Fréchet derivative solving the linearized Beltrami equation. On the Orlicz heart $E^Φ_{\mathcal{U}}(\mathbb{C})$ it is real $C^\infty$, yet fails to be real analytic at zero: along any direction $h$, its Taylor series at zero has radius of convergence $1/\|h\|_\infty$ in $W^{1,2}(B)$ for every disk $B\supset\overline{\mathcal{U}}$. Finally, for $\mathcal{U}=\mathbb{D}$, the exterior Schwarzian map from $E^Φ_{\mathbb{D}}(\mathbb{C})$ to the little logarithmic Bers space is continuous, but fails to be Fréchet differentiable at zero; moreover, its zero fiber is not a $C^1$ embedded Banach submanifold near zero, obstructing any local $C^1$ split submersion structure on the resulting quotient.

♻ ☆ The virial--Kato method and the asymptotic stability of solitons of the generalized Benjamin, Bona and Mahony equation

We prove that every orbitally stable soliton of the pure-power generalized Benjamin--Bona--Mahony (gBBM) equation is locally asymptotically stable. For both nonlinearities $f(u)=|u|^{p-1}u$ and $f(u)=|u|^p$, the result holds for every exponent $p>1$ throughout the orbital stability range $c>c^*(p)$. Solutions starting sufficiently close to one of these solitons in the energy space converge locally in a moving frame to a nearby soliton and the limiting soliton has a speed close to that of the initial soliton. This establishes, for pure-power gBBM, the local convergence predicted by Bona and Soyeur's asymptotic stability conjecture and addresses an open problem raised by Martel. The proof uses Kato smoothing to close the high-energy virial estimates. The required smoothing estimates rely on the absence of nonzero embedded eigenvalues of the linearized operator. We establish this spectral property for every $p>1$ and every soliton speed $c>1$, including speeds for which the soliton is orbitally unstable. This settles a Pego--Weinstein spectral conjecture in the pure-power gBBM case.

☆ Rank 1 composition factors in the polydisk

Denoting its corresponding Hilbert space by $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$, we define the rank of $φ$ with respect to $k$ as the dimension of $\mathcal{H}(k^φ)$. Using these notions, we reframe recent work considering co-isometric weighted composition operators in the unit disk by Mas, Martín, and Vukotić, and in the unit ball by Hartz and Tornes. That is, we illustrate a bijective correspondence between the above operators and rank $1$ composition operators, and extend their results to the setting of the polydisk. Namely, supposing that $φ$ is a rank $1$ composition factor of $k$ and assuming that $k$ is either bounded or unbounded everywhere on $\partial\mathbb{D}^d$, we prove that $φ$ must be an automorphism. Moreover, if it is not a composition of a rotation and permutation, then $k$ must be a positive power of the Szegő kernel. We also briefly consider finite rank composition factors.

☆ A characterization of almost everywhere convergence of subsequences of Walsh--Fourier partial sums
Weisz Ferenc, Guangheng Xie, Dachun Yang
We characterize the increasing sequences $(ν_j)$ in the set of positive integers $\mathbb N$ along which the Walsh--Fourier partial sums $s_{ν_j}(f)$ of every integrable function $f$ converge almost everywhere to $f$. This resolves a problem that Konyagin posed in his invited address at the 2006 International Congress of Mathematicians~\cite{K06}. The criterion concerns the binary expansions of the integers $ν_j$. Divide each $ν_j$ by $2^k$. Convergence holds if and only if, for some $K\in\mathbb N$, the number of distinct positive quotients whose remainder has binary variation larger than $K$ is bounded independently of the scale $k$. This is also equivalent to the weak type $(1,1)$ inequality for $\sup_{j\in\mathbb N}|s_{ν_j}(f)|$, and if the criterion fails, then the partial sums of some integrable function along $(ν_j)$ are unbounded at every point. The criterion contains the bounded variation condition and Konyagin's condition for separated spectra, and we give examples, for convergence and for divergence, that are not covered by the earlier results.

☆ The Commutant of the Adjoint Center Need Not Be the Center of the Dual
Hülya Duru, Arkady Kitover, Mehmet Orhon
Let $X$ be a Banach lattice with ideal center $Z(X)$, and let $Z^*(X)=\{S^*:S\in Z(X)\}$ be the set of adjoints of central operators, acting on the dual $X^*$. The center $Z(X^*)$ of the dual is always contained in the commutant $(Z^*(X))^{\mathrm{com}}$ of $Z^*(X)$, and equality is known when $X$ has a topological order unit. It has been asserted that equality holds whenever $X$ has a topologically full center; the published proof of this assertion is incorrect, and the question has been recorded as open. We show that the assertion is false. The construction rests on a general sufficient condition, proved with an invariant mean taking values in a Dedekind complete space $C(K)$ and the injectivity of $C(K)$. We also collect positive results and a norm-density criterion for equality. For every Orlicz space $L_Φ$ we show that every operator in $(Z^*(L_Φ))^{\mathrm{com}}$ is lower-triangular with respect to the decomposition of the dual into its order continuous and singular bands, with central diagonal entries, and, by a splitting lemma based on Young's inequality, that the off-diagonal entry vanishes. Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

For bounded spatial and frequency sets $A,B\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ of positive measure with finite upper codimension-one Minkowski boundary content, the number $Λ_\varepsilon(cA,B)$ of eigenvalues in $(\varepsilon,1-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $Λ_\varepsilon(cA,B)\le C(d,A,B,β)c^{d-1}D(1+\log_+(c/D))$, where $D=\log(1/(\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)))$, for every fixed $β>0$, $c\ge2$, $0<\varepsilon<1/2$, and $D\leβc$, with $\log_+t=\max(0,\log t)$. The argument uses positive band-limited smoothing and requires no symmetry, convexity, or connectedness. In dimension two, the corresponding exponential-window estimate has a constant uniform in the window parameter. We also determine the optimal coordinate-Lipschitz constant $d-1$ for recursive decompositions of balls and standard simplices in every dimension, and obtain box-frequency estimates with explicit geometric constants. For $C^1$ convex bodies in three dimensions, the optimal infimum of recursive coordinate slopes is $2$. Uniform real-order Bessel estimates give independent disk and ball bounds at every spectral threshold, including an explicit deep-tail term. For smooth strictly convex planar frequency bodies with positive curvature, we prove correlation estimates for aligned Gaussian packets at arbitrary relative scales and quantitative lower bounds on the cost of estimating spatial blocks separately. Together these results connect the global spectral bound with sharp geometric constructions and the cancellation retained by grouping boundary interactions.

☆ Analytical solution of general interface problems for reaction-advection-diffusion equations
Andreas Chatziafratis, Guenbo Hwang, Georgia Karali
We obtain novel integral representations, expressed as contour integrals in the complex Fourier plane, for the solution of fully nonhomogeneous interface problems for classical reaction-advection-diffusion (RAD) equations with arbitrary initial data on the line and general interface conditions at the origin. Such problems of applied mathematics emerge in a spectacular variety of physical phenomena in mathematical physics, chemistry, continuum mechanics, biology, pharmacokinetics, as well as mathematical finance. A suitable implementation of Fokas' unified transform method is in force herein, with particular challenges arising due to inclusion in the model of lower-order terms, and the generality of interface problems under consideration. To our knowledge, this careful analysis has not appeared in (nor does it follow easily from) literature published so far. Our explicit formulae directly lend themselves to explorations of solutions' qualitative properties such as regularity, asymptotic behavior and well-posedness. This work has also been of utility in the investigation of nonlinear counterparts as well as in the study of phase-transition phenomena, moving-interface and diffuse-interface problems. Such results for RAD and high-order PDEs will soon appear in a series of separate papers.
☆ On the linearization of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation in $\mathbb{R}^N$
Massimo Grossi, Sérgio L. N Neves, Zoe Saudade Wynants
Let $u$ be a positive radial solution of the supercritical Lane-Emden equation $$-Δu=u^p \qquad \text{in }\mathbb{R}^N, \qquad p>\frac{N+2}{N-2}. $$ In this paper we classify the bounded solutions of the associated linearized operator $-Δw -pu^{p-1}w=0$ in $\mathbb{R}^N$. The resulting classification reveals the role of the threshold value $p=\frac{N + \sqrt{N^2 - 8N}}{4}$. In particular, above this threshold, the solutions are generated by the invariance of the problem under dilations and translations. Below this threshold, many new solutions appear, and their number tends to infinity as $p$ approaches the Joseph-Lundgren exponent and $N$ is large.

In this paper we prove the existence of self-similar solutions to the capillary water wave problem. In particular, this implies finite-time formation of singularities in the form of a corner, and retraction from a corner due to the time-reversibility of the equations. Unlike most self-similar smooth solutions, the solutions with $2/3$ time-length scaling are seen in experiments like pinch-off retraction, bubble bursting or jet formation. The proof involves a new argument through the regularization of the Hamiltonian and does not require the existence of an approximate profile. We believe this strategy has further implications in the construction of self-similar solutions of dispersive PDE.

Let $X\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be a subanalytic set of dimension $d\ge 2$, closed near $0$, with an isolated singularity at $0$ and connected link, whose regular part carries the induced Riemannian metric. We study harmonic functions on $X\setminus\{0\}$ near $0$. (i) If $X$ is bi-Lipschitz equivalent, for the intrinsic metric, to a generalized horn $\{(z^γy,z):\ y\in L,\ z\ge 0\}$, with $γ\ge 1$ rational and $L$ compact, connected, subanalytic and analytic, then: - every bounded harmonic function extends continuously to $0$; - every positive harmonic function near $0$ can be written as $qG_X+u_b$, with $q\ge 0$, $u_b$ bounded and $G_X$ a fixed singular profile; - a Bôcher-type theorem holds: a positive harmonic function is either bounded or tends to $+\infty$, and two divergent ones have a nontrivial linear combination that extends continuously. The proof relies on a volume doubling and weak Poincaré condition on intrinsic balls away from $0$, invariant under bi-Lipschitz homeomorphisms, which together with an annular connectedness condition implies a Harnack inequality on annuli; the decomposition then follows from a Picard-principle argument whose geometric input is the Harnack inequality on the links. (ii) If $d\ge 3$ and the spherical blow-up of $X$ at $0$ is a regular manifold with boundary parametrizing $X$ near $0$ (condition (R) of the paper), the singular profile has a polyhomogeneous expansion, which is described and may contain a $\logρ$ term, $ρ=|x|$. (iii) For the rotational cusps $|x|^2=z^m$, $m>2$, $d\ge 3$, whose spherical blow-up is not regular, the profile is radial of order $ρ^{1-m(d-1)/2}$, so that its exponent depends on the rate at which the sections shrink.

Starting from any compact sub-extremal Schwarzschild-de Sitter region with positive cosmological constant, we construct a family of static axisymmetric vacuum solutions with two additional black-hole horizons, each of prescribed area. All horizons and the symmetry axis are regular, and the metric and lapse are real analytic up to the boundary. As the mass parameter tends to zero, the metric and lapse converge smoothly to the reference solution away from two antipodal points on its sphere of maximal lapse. Rescaling near either added horizon yields the Schwarzschild spatial metric in the limit. For small prescribed mass, the lapse attains its maximum precisely on one equatorial circle. Its Hessian is negative definite in the transverse plane, with the smaller eigenvalue magnitude asymptotic to a positive constant times the added mass. Nearby regular level sets are tori. The proof combines gluing at separated scales with uniform elliptic estimates. An integral condition removes infinitesimal translations of each Schwarzschild model, while a localized tensor source restores solvability of the linearized equation. Matching the local Schwarzschild corrections to a global Green tensor identifies the leading source coefficients. Reflection makes these coefficients equal, and varying the common radial position of the centers makes them vanish. A radial Green function and the heat equation on the sphere determine the angular variation of the lapse and the geometry of its maximum set.

☆ Symmetries, conservation laws, series solutions and singularity formation for the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations in mass coordinates
Adnan Shamaoon
Written in Lagrangian mass coordinates, the spherically symmetric Euler-Poisson equations for a polytropic gas become a single second-order equation for the radius $r(t,m)$ of the shell enclosing mass $m$, with adiabatic index $γ>1$ and entropy profile $S(m)$. We determine all point symmetries of this equation. Apart from time translation there is at most one scaling, except at the critical index $γ=4/3$, where a scaling exists for every entropy profile; these scalings are the entropy-fixed stabilisers of the two-parameter scaling group of the non-isentropic system, and we give the exact symmetry defect when $γ\neq4/3$. Noether's theorem singles out the profiles $S=Km^{14-10γ}$, for which a scaling is variational and gives a conservation law beyond energy; otherwise the scalings yield virial identities. We construct exact collapse solutions and reduce the self-similar problem to one ordinary differential equation. Using the Briot-Bouquet theorem we prove that the regular centre of self-similar and homologous collapse carries a convergent analytic expansion with free central amplitude, and we derive a Puiseux expansion at the stellar surface whose exponent is the polytropic index $1/(γ-1)$. In mass coordinates a density singularity is a zero of $r_m$ or of $r$; for the first kind we prove a Hopf-type fold law and an exact shell-crossing criterion for free-falling dust. Finally, linear perturbations of the critical Einstein-de Sitter collapse separate exactly into spherical Bessel profiles, with exponents solving $3κ^2+κ-2+μ=0$. All identities were checked by computer algebra, and the numerical statements rest on convergence studies of a second-order Lagrangian scheme, including a collapse with a free surface.

Jan-Frederik Pietschmann, Carmen Tretmans, Nicola Zamponi
We derive and analyze a phase-field model describing the formation of the active layer of organic solar cells. The process combines phase separation of an electron donor (polymer) and an electron acceptor (non-fullerene acceptor) with evaporation of a solvent. Taking the macroscopic motion of the fluid into account, this results in a coupled system of incompressible Navier--Stokes, degenerate multispecies Cahn--Hilliard, and Allen--Cahn equations with cross-diffusion terms. We give a thermodynamically consistent derivation of the system and prove the existence of global-in-time weak solutions without any size constraints on the data. The solutions dissipate the total energy and require an ad-hoc variational formulation of the definition of the diffusion fluxes, which is made necessary by the degeneracy of the mobility matrix.

For coefficients with fixed interior support and uniform Sobolev bounds, the data determine the exterior derivative of the drift and a gauge-invariant reaction term with a logarithmic modulus. Prescribing the divergence gives separate stability for the drift and reaction coefficients. The input and observation patches may be arbitrary nonempty open subsets of the same or opposite faces. The proof combines a quantitative passage from finite-time responses to a stationary boundary map with a Runge approximation estimate in the measured $H^{3/2}$ input norm. The first step uses sectorial semigroups on the unbounded slab; the second transfers the partial data to a full boundary map on an interior domain, where magnetic stability estimates apply. We also prove conditional stability for boundary-touching supports and uniqueness from one encoded input with unknown initial state. A tracer-transport application identifies an incompressible velocity and a reaction-loss coefficient.

For short-range kernels, instead, the negative phase may enter the box, and the positive phase may be disconnected. Moreover, if the datum is $-1$ around the box and $+1$ only at distance two from it, the configuration identically $-1$ is perceptive at every boundary site of the box for fractional kernels with small exponent.

By transforming the problem into a nonlocal moving-boundary problem, we show that the associated Poincaré map is strongly positive and power compact, which yields existence and uniqueness of the principal eigenvalue and several variational characterizations. To the best of our knowledge, this spectral theory is new even in \textbf{the scalar case}. We then apply these results to nonlinear systems. On bounded intervals, the sign of the principal eigenvalue gives a sharp dichotomy: solutions either converge to a unique positive time-periodic solution or vanish as time tends to infinity. We also prove convergence of positive periodic solutions as the interval expands. For the Cauchy problem on the whole real line, we characterize the leftward and rightward spreading speeds, which may differ for asymmetric dispersal kernels, and establish necessary and sufficient conditions for accelerated spreading in either direction. ☆ Stability and bifurcation of shrinking spheres for the fractional mean curvature flow

Below $n_*$, the two-dimensional diffusion-map reading carries an existence guarantee; above $n_*$ the guarantee lapses, and this lapse does not rule out a slow manifold. The closed form for $n_*$ follows from the reaction Lipschitz constant and the slow-mode growth rate. The certificate is tested on a quadratic and a cubic model system. At the Brusselator boundary the existence sign is checked by interval enclosure, and the spectral margin decays as $n^{-4}$ across the transition. On strongly damped Hopf lattices the slow manifold collapses to the uniform limit cycle; this degeneracy, the trivial graph $\varphi\equiv0$, is reported directly rather than concealed. The boundary gives a PDE-side prior for data-driven reduction: it marks the resolution at which a recovered two-dimensional structure can be trusted.

This paper investigates the existence, multiplicity and asymptotic behavior of solutions to a class of nonlocal logistic-type problems with the \(r\)-Laplacian operator in the fast diffusion regime: %, with a real parameter $λ$: \[ \begin{cases} -Δ_r u - \displaystyle\int_Ω K(x,y)u(y)\,dy = a(x)u +λ|u|^{q-2}u \displaystyle\int_ΩQ(x,y)|u(y)|^q\,dy, & x\in Ω, \\[0.4em] u = 0, & x\in \partialΩ. \end{cases} \] The model has local diffusion, nonlocal dispersal, and nonlinear global interactions, and depends on a real parameter $λ$. For $λ\ge 0$, we establish the existence of nonnegative weak solutions via a variational principle. In the case \(λ<0\), we characterize two variational thresholds, \(-\infty<\widehatλ^*<λ^*<0\), which separate different solution intervals. For \(λ^*<λ<0\), the energy functional has a global minimizer with negative energy and a mountain-pass critical point with positive energy, yielding two distinct nontrivial weak solutions. The same holds at \(λ=λ^*\), where the global minimizer has zero energy. In a left neighborhood of \(λ^*\), two distinct nontrivial weak solutions persist, a local minimizer and a mountain-pass critical point, both with positive energy and the latter at a strictly higher level. For \(λ<\widehatλ^*\), only the trivial solution exists. Finally, as $λ\to 0^-$, the norm of the global minimizers blows up. Along subsequences, selected nonnegative mountain-pass solutions converge strongly in $W_0^{1,r}(Ω)$ as $λ\to 0$ to a nontrivial nonnegative weak solution of the problem at $λ= 0$. The associated mountain-pass levels converge to the same limit from both sides of zero, and the corresponding solution norms also converge to a common value.

For nonnegative segregated initial data, we classify the limits for all exponents at least one under homogeneous Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. The limiting equations include the heat equation, a one-phase Stefan problem, a fixed-domain heat equation, and a nonlinear equation with a time-integral reaction term. We also describe the limiting behavior of the nondiffusing component and obtain a nontrivial rescaled limit. In the critical regime, we characterize the limit as the greatest weak solution and establish a transition between initial finite propagation and instantaneous positivity. Under Dirichlet conditions, permanent zero regions may occur for certain small initial data.
comment: 25 pages
☆ Inviscid limit of steady Navier--Stokes equations with Navier friction boundary conditions in a periodic channel
Robin Ming Chen, Dehua Wang, Weiqiang Wang
The vanishing viscosity limit of the steady incompressible Navier--Stokes equations is studied in a periodic channel with Navier friction boundary conditions, where the slip length is assumed to be a nonnegative power of the viscosity. Depending on this power, the problem falls into subcritical, critical, and supercritical regimes. In each regime, the Navier--Stokes solutions are constructed via the Prandtl expansion, and the validity of the expansion is rigorously justified. By the Prandtl--Batchelor theory, the leading Euler solution is a Couette flow, and the interaction between the interior and boundary-layer profiles is precisely characterized. Of particular interest is the critical regime, in which the leading order Prandtl profile solves a nonlinear steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition. The well-posedness of this problem is established using the von Mises transformation and the implicit function theorem, and an implicit Batchelor--Wood formula is derived that determines the coefficients of the leading order Couette flow from the boundary data. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first well-posedness result for the steady Prandtl equation with a Robin-type boundary condition.
comment: 57 pages. All comments are welcome
☆ Sharp History-Length Dependence of Mesh-Uniform Exponential Decay Rates for a Boundary-Memory Euler-Bernoulli Beam
Gossrin Jean-Marc Bomisso
For a boundary-memory Euler--Bernoulli beam with polynomial relaxation, we quantify the loss of exponential stability as the retained history length $S$ grows. The continuous and conforming Hermite--$\mathbb P_1$ generators have zero-frequency resolvent norms bounded above and below by constant multiples of $S$. The bounds are uniform in the beam mesh and in every history mesh of step at most a fixed $h_0$. Their semigroup norms retain a plateau of duration proportional to $S$. Under positive distributed and boundary damping, matching exponential estimates hold with the optimal time scale $1+S$, uniformly in the meshes. Optimality refers to the semigroup norm on the augmented state space, which includes the history. Without distributed damping, the same time scale holds for the continuous truncated generator under a boundary condition on $δ^{(3)}$. We also prove strong convergence of the finite-history semigroups to the full-history semigroup, uniformly on compact time intervals, under restriction and zero extension of histories. Remote-history packets give residuals of order $S^{-1}$ for the truncated generator and of order $S^{-1}+h$ after discretization, improved to $S^{-1}$ at zero frequency. Numerical tests confirm the residual orders.
comment: 18 pages, 4 figures
☆ Local Reynolds number criteria for the regularity of the three-dimensional Navier-Stokes equations, and their consistency with forced finite-time blow-up
Ali Bouzekri
We give four regularity criteria for the forced Navier-Stokes equations in $\mathbb{R}^3$. The first is an $\dot H^1$ estimate: a strong solution cannot blow up while the local Reynolds number $|v|^2/(ν|ω|)$ stays below $4/(3\sqrt3)$ wherever the vorticity exceeds a threshold $M(t)$ with $\int M^{6/5}\,dt<\infty$. It rests on an exact identity that gives the cubic vorticity term a favorable sign. Two further $\dot H^1$ estimates use the Newton potential of $|ω|^2$, either as a multiplier or as a gradient added to the Lamb vector, so that the integral of $|ω|^2|v|^2$ cancels. The second of these gives a critical condition on the vorticity alone, implied by $\int\|ω\|_{L^3}^2\,dt<\infty$. The fourth is a maximum principle for $\frac12|v|^2+λ|ω|$: vortex stretching is absorbed by viscous dissipation, and the pressure is controlled by a weighted local estimate. It requires a bound on $|v|^2/(ν|\nabla v|)$ only at maximum points where the velocity part dominates. We show that the forced finite-time blow-up recently constructed by OpenAI violates each hypothesis, and that the violations locate its mechanism: inflow down the centripetal pressure gradient, at the same order as viscous dissipation.
☆ Airy Path Integral Representation for the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili Equation
Jeremy Quastel, C. Alexander Rodriguez
We give a representation for solutions of the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili II (KP-II) equation as path integrals over the Airy line ensemble. The initial condition enters directly as a potential, bypassing the usual direct and inverse scattering constructions. We establish the representation for broad classes of signed initial data, prove uniqueness in specified solution classes, and derive a restart identity expressing solutions as Airy path integrals of their own earlier states. For arbitrary real $L^2$ initial data, a centered version of the Airy occupation represents the standard global KP-II flow. We show how the representation recovers the classical Marchenko determinant for Korteweg-de Vries (KdV), and identify a Brownian-path amplitude with the classical KP-II heat-scattering coefficient. We obtain explicit formulas for soliton solutions and derive KP from a Toda equation for nonintersecting Brownian bridges. Finally, we use the restart identity to characterize one-point distributions of the KPZ fixed point through their singular initial conditions, and derive sharp lower-tail asymptotics directly from KP.
comment: 120 pages, 4 figures. Comments welcome
☆ Exterior $p$-capacitary rigidity on groups of Heisenberg type
Federica Dragoni, Nicola Garofalo, Gianmarco Giovannardi, Paolo Salani, Dimiter Vassilev
We study the exterior Bernoulli overdetermined problem for sub-elliptic operators. Let $\mathbb{G}$ be a group of Heisenberg type with Property (H), and let $Ω\subset \mathbb{G}$ be a domain enjoying a partial symmetry property and containing a Korányi-Kaplan ball $\overline{B_r}$ centered at the origin. We consider a function $u$ that is $p$-harmonic with respect to the $p$-sub-Laplacian $Δ_{\mathbb{G},p}$ in the annular region $Ω\setminus \overline{B}_r$, satisfying the boundary conditions $ u = 0 \;\text{ on }\; \partialΩ, \quad u = 1 \;\text{ on }\; \partial B_r.$ We show that if $p$ is even and $u$ satisfies a mild overdetermined condition on the sub-Riemannian norm of its gradient on the outer boundary $\partialΩ$, then $Ω$ must itself be a Korányi--Kaplan ball centered at the origin, and $u$ is the corresponding normalized capacitary potential; equivalently, away from the pole it is an affine normalization of the fundamental solution of $Δ_{\mathbb{G},p}$.
☆ Localization and homogenization of anisotropic fractional energies
Julián Fernández Bonder, Ariel Salort
We study the joint limit of localization ($s\uparrow1$) and periodic homogenization ($\varepsilon\downarrow0$) for anisotropic fractional energies with $p$-growth and oscillating kernels. We prove that the $Γ$-limit is governed by the single parameter $θ=\lim\varepsilon^{p(1-s)}$, and that its density is the convex combination $θ\mathcal{A}^* + (1-θ)\bar{\mathcal{A}}$ of the homogenized and the averaged densities. This shows that the picture recently obtained for quadratic energies also holds for every $p$ and for anisotropic kernels, with no regularity in the oscillating variable; the approach is different, and is based on convex duality. A nonlocal version of the duality argument gives the limit as $s\uparrow 1$ for a fixed kernel under weak assumptions, correcting a previous proof by the authors.
☆ Rupture and far-field profiles for Hénon-type MEMS elliptic equation with pressure
Yunxiao Li, Yanyan Zhang
Motivated by membrane touchdown in electrostatic microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) under external pressure, we study the Hénon-type elliptic equation $Δu=λ|x|^αu^{-p}+F$, $u>0$, where $N\ge2$, $λ,p>0$, $α>-2$, $F\in\mathbb R$, and $α<2p$ if $F\ne0$. Near the origin, we construct positive radial rupture solutions with $u(0)=0$ for $F\ne0$ and infinitely many non-radial but asymptotically radial ones for every $F$, and derive expansions to arbitrary order. On exterior domains $Ω_{R_0}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^N:|x|>R_0\}$, with no condition at the origin, we establish existence and uniqueness of positive solutions on $[R_0,\infty)$ for radial initial value problems with $u(R_0)>0$ if $p\ge1$, or if $F\ge0$ and $u'(R_0)\ge0$. We determine the leading behavior of all positive radial exterior solutions as $|x|\to\infty$ for $F>0$ and $F=0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$ and $α\ge0$. For possibly non-radial exterior solutions satisfying $u(r,θ)=A_\infty r^{σ_\infty}(1+o(1))$ uniformly in $θ$, with $A_\infty>0$ and $σ_\infty\in\mathbb R$, we uniquely determine the leading exponent and coefficient in all three pressure regimes, without derivative bounds on the remainder. Although pressure affects only higher-order terms near an asymptotically radial rupture point, its sign changes the leading-order behavior at infinity under the stated hypotheses. Local radial rupture solutions extend uniquely to $\mathbb R^N\setminus\{0\}$ for $F>0$, and for $F<0$ when $p\ge1$, with the classified far-field profiles under the corresponding hypotheses.

♻ ☆ Interior $W^{2,p}$ regularity for the $k$-Hessian equation

For densities bounded above and below by positive constants, we establish $W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,1}$ regularity for continuous $k$-convex solutions; the exponent $1$ is optimal even for constant density. Higher interior regularity holds under either of two assumptions: $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,k(k-1)/2}$, or $u\in C_{\mathrm{loc}}^{1,β}$ for some $1-2/k<β<1$. Under either assumption, if the density is positive and continuous, then $u\in W_{\mathrm{loc}}^{2,p}$ for every $1
♻ ☆ Reconstruction of non-self-adjoint anisotropic and complex inclusions in the Calderón problem
Henrik Garde, David Johansson, Thanasis Zacharopoulos
We generalize recent results on the monotonicity method, for inclusion detection in the partial data anisotropic Calderón problem, to very general non-self-adjoint perturbations. This involves a forward model that accounts for both the anisotropic real conductivity and the anisotropic permittivity, and the results hold in any spatial dimension $d\geq 2$. We assume that the inclusion boundaries can be reached from the domain boundary via a set on which the background conductivity is self-adjoint, and that a definiteness condition holds near the inclusion boundaries. Away from the inclusion boundaries we allow general $L^\infty$ non-self-adjoint perturbations. We only require unique continuation based on the self-adjoint part of the background conductivity, thus making the methods compatible with generic unique continuation results.
comment: 16 pages
♻ ☆ Global Strong Solutions and Large-Time Behavior for Radial Compressible Navier-Stokes Flow with Density-Dependent Viscosities on a Disk and in the Plane
Kexin Li
The two-dimensional barotropic compressible Navier-Stokes equations admit a unique global strong solution for arbitrarily large compatible radial initial data without swirl and with density bounded away from zero, both on a disk with a no-slip wall and in the whole plane. The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. For each exponent in this range, the bulk viscosity coefficient may take any nonnegative value. This is the full range allowed by nonnegative viscous dissipation in a two-dimensional Newtonian fluid with positive shear viscosity. Every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, these results apply to Marche's viscous shallow water equations on a flat bottom in the absence of rotation, bottom friction, and capillarity. These equations retain the positive second viscosity derived from free-surface flow and thus fall outside the Bresch-Desjardins relation. The density remains uniformly bounded above and away from zero for all time. On the disk, the density and velocity converge exponentially in the Sobolev norm of order three to the spatial mean of the density and to zero, respectively. In the plane, the solution converges in the same norm to the prescribed far-field state with positive density and zero velocity. The same conclusions hold for classes of non-power viscosities, including laws with different growth rates at low and high density.
comment: 68 pages. The global strong solution results now include the case of zero bulk viscosity on both the disk and the plane
♻ ☆ Shallow-water convergence of the intermediate long wave equation in $L^2$
Andreia Chapouto, Guopeng Li, Tadahiro Oh, Tengfei Zhao
We continue our study on the convergence issue of the intermediate long wave equation (ILW) on both the real line and the circle. In particular, we establish convergence of the scaled ILW dynamics to that of the Korteweg-de Vries equation (KdV) in the shallow-water limit at the $L^2$-level. Together with the recent work by the first three authors and D. Pilod (2024) on the deep-water convergence in $L^2$, this work completes the well-posedness and convergence study of ILW on both geometries within the $L^2$-framework. Our proof equally applies to both geometries and is based on the following two ingredients: the complete integrability of ILW and the normal form method. More precisely, by making use of the Lax pair structure and the perturbation determinant for ILW, recently introduced by Harrop-Griffths, Killip, and Vişan (2026), we first establish weakly uniform (in small depth parameters) equicontinuity in $L^2$ of solutions to the scaled ILW, providing a control on the high frequency part of solutions. Then, we treat the low frequency part by implementing a perturbative argument based on an infinite iteration of normal form reductions for KdV.
comment: 51 pages. We corrected an error in Section 4 and made minor updates. To appear in Proc. Lond. Math. Soc
♻ ☆ Well-posedness and long-time behavior for self-consistent Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations with general potentials
Pierre Gervais, Maxime Herda
We study the well-posedness, steady states and long time behavior of solutions to Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation with external confinement potential and nonlinear self-consistent interactions. Our analysis introduces newly characterized conditions on the interaction kernel that ensure the local asymptotic stability of the unique steady state. Compared to previous works on this topic, our results allow for large, singular and non-symmetric interactions. As a corollary of our main results, we show exponential decay of solutions to the Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation in dimension $3$, for low regularity initial data. In the repulsive case, the result holds in strongly nonlinear regimes (i.e. for arbitrarily small Debye length). Our techniques rely on the design of new Lyapunov functionals based on hypocoercivity and hypoellipticity theories. We use norms which include part of the interaction kernel, and carefully mix ``macroscopic quantities based''--hypocoercivity with ``commutators based''--hypocoercivity.
♻ ☆ A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
Iryna Karpenko, Dmitry Shepelsky, Gerald Teschl
We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate right and left matrix Riemann--Hilbert problems and derive parametric formulas for reconstructing both components. These formulas also use a transported profile determined by the initial ratio of the two momenta. Under suitable regularity and positivity assumptions, we show that a solution of the right Riemann--Hilbert problem, together with this profile, yields a local solution of the 2-mCH system. For a common constant background, we construct a family of smooth reflectionless solutions associated with a single pair of discrete eigenvalues. The scalar soliton, obtained when the profile vanishes, is the only travelling wave in this family.
comment: 50 pages, 1 figure
♻ ☆ Riesz Transform Bounds Imply Parabolic Uniform Rectifiability of Graphs
John Hoffman
We prove that if a $(k+2)$-Ahlfors--David regular measure $μ$ in parabolic space $\mathbb P^n$ has support equal to a parabolic Lipschitz graph with sufficiently small Lipschitz constant, and the parabolic Riesz transform is bounded on $L^2(μ)$, then $μ$ is parabolic uniformly rectifiable and the graph is regular parabolic Lipschitz. The result holds for every integer $0\leq k\leq n-1$.
comment: 97 pages
♻ ☆ Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for Hamilton--Jacobi equations with supercritical viscosity
Gengyu Liu, Zibo Wang, Jianlu Zhang
This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $σ>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^σΔu_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{σ-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality therein.

♻ ☆ Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
Pascal Auscher
We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
comment: Addition of a reference posted right after this post and a comment in the introduction.Maths are unchanged
♻ ☆ Eventual Collisional Relaxation After Large Echo-Driven Amplification in a Weakly Collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck System
Luo Yue
We study the weakly collisional Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck system near a Maxwellian equilibrium and construct global classical solutions exhibiting large transient growth before eventual collisional relaxation. The main mechanism is a nonlinear plasma-echo cascade which remains effective up to the enhanced-dissipation time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$, producing norm inflation of size larger than $ν^{-1}$ from arbitrarily small $ν$-dependent perturbations. At the same time, the nonzero spatial modes decay at the enhanced-dissipation scale $e^{-\mathsf{r}ν^{\frac13}t}$, while the zero mode relaxes at the thermal scale $e^{-νt}$. The estimates also reveal a sharp contrast in the smoothing effects before and after the collisional time scale $t\sim ν^{-1}$. As a consequence, our construction gives explicit upper bounds on the Sobolev and Gevrey stability thresholds: perturbations of the corresponding $ν$-dependent sizes can still trigger severe echo-driven amplification before collisional dissipation becomes dominant at the critical time scale $t\simν^{-\frac13}$.
♻ ☆ Rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully nonlinear extrinsic geometric flows: Classification and Applications
José Torres Santaella
We study rotationally symmetric translating solitons of fully non-linear extrinsic geometric flows in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ driven by positive $α$-homogeneous curvature functions, building on Rengaswami's classification of bowl-type translators. For positive ends at infinity and every $α>0$, we derive two correction terms beyond the leading order in the nondegenerate case and the growth rate in each degenerate regime. Imposing the translator equation across the neck on a signed extension of the curvature function, we construct catenoidal translators and classify their continuations according to a branch of the rotational level set. These yield complete embedded translators or maximal pieces, for which we determine the regularity at each transition and the shrinking-neck asymptotics; each alternative is realized in a model family of curvature functions. As applications of the tangency principle, we obtain rigidity and nonexistence results governed by the global geometry of the bowl-type solutions. When the bowl is entire, it is unique up to vertical translation among convex translators with a single graphical end asymptotic to it (also under a weighted condition in the strictly convex case), and its existence rules out both convex translating graphs over bounded domains that blow up at the boundary and entire ones growing uniformly faster or slower than the bowl. When the bowl is not entire, it may have finite height for $α>1$; in this setting, any strictly convex translating graph over a ball that is continuous up to the boundary and has vertical tangent planes there is necessarily a bowl of finite height.
comment: Comments are welcome!
♻ ☆ A tree-like fractal Dirichlet space lying between strong and weak elliptic Harnack inequalities
Caoxu Huang, Guanhua Liu
In this paper we construct a self-similar fractal configured as an infinitely branched tree and equip it with a regular self-similar Dirichlet form. Fixing a typical metric ball, we compute accurately the effective resistance between an inner point and the boundary of this ball. Based on this result, anomalous behaviour of the mean exit time from such balls is shown -- the ratio between whose supremum and infimum can be arbitrarily large. Under properly selected self-similar measure, we further show the weak elliptic Harnack inequality holds but the strong analogue fails.
♻ ☆ A Construction of Cauchy Data for Trapped Surface Formation in the Massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon System

We construct a class of smooth, spherically symmetric, asymptotically flat Cauchy data for the massive Einstein--Klein--Gordon system that are initially untrapped but give rise to trapped surface formation in their maximal Cauchy developments. These data coincide with contracting Friedmann--Lemaître--Robertson--Walker (FLRW) data on an interior ball and with Schwarzschild data outside a larger ball. The data can also be made to have arbitrarily small compactness: the ratio $2m/r$, where $m$ is the Hawking mass and $r$ is the area radius, can be made arbitrarily small throughout the initial Cauchy hypersurface.

♻ ☆ Operator dependent para-controlled calculus, periodic homogenisation and singular PDEs
Yilin Chen, Weijun Xu
We develop a variant of the para-controlled distributions framework based on operator dependent (generalised) Besov spaces. This in particular covers the class of oscillatory operators from periodic homogenisation. We then apply the framework to study periodic homogenisation problems for a class of singular stochastic PDEs. One novel viewpoint is to measure regularity via the geometry induced by the operators at hand rather than classical Fourier basis. The generalised Besov spaces were introduced by Kerkyacharian-Petrushev. In contrast to the Fourier decomposition in the classical setting, they are built from spectral decomposition of general self-adjoint elliptic operators. A major difference is that products of two spectrally localised functions in general have ``frequencies" spread over the whole spectrum. We obtain a decay estimate on ``high frequency" component of the product of two spectrally-localised functions. This enables us to obtain uniform bounds for the naturally associated para-product and commutator operations over a class of operators. This in particular includes the family of periodic homogenisation operators uniform in the oscillation parameter. Next, we show convergence properties of these operations in the periodic homogenisation setting. A key ingredient is a sharp quantitative convergence of the generalised Littlewood-Paley block operators. The proof utilises the Helffer-Sjöstrand's formula for self-adjoint operators. Finally, we apply this framework to periodic homogenisation problems for dynamical $φ^4_3$, $2$D gPAM, and $1$D KPZ. Assuming the convergence of stochastic objects to their homogenised limits, we show that the solutions and fluxes also converge to the corresponding limits. The convergence of the explicit stochastic terms with suitable renormalisations will be treated in a separate note.

♻ ☆ Isolated singularities of solutions to the Yamabe equation with boundary in higher dimensions I
Yuxuan Liao
We study isolated boundary singularities of positive solutions of the scalar-flat boundary Yamabe equation. We prove the critical upper bound for general smooth metrics in dimensions $3\le n\le17$ and for Euclidean domains with smooth boundary in dimensions $3\le n\le22$. For general metrics, this range extends to $n=18$ when the conformal metric is complete near the singularity. In every dimension, the critical upper bound implies removability or a matching lower bound and convergence to a unique flat Fowler solution with a positive power rate. Sharpness of these dimension ranges will be established in a subsequent paper.

We investigate the isotropic $L_p$ Minkowski problem in $\mathbb{R}^n$ for $p<-n$. We prove that a smooth strictly convex solution $K$ is the unit ball if the second non-zero eigenvalue of the Hilbert-Brunn-Minkowski operator satisfies $λ_2(-L_K)\ge\frac{-p-1}{n-1}$. We also derive a lower bound for $λ_2(-L_K)$ in terms of concentric inner and outer ellipsoids and give improved bounds for origin-centred and origin-symmetric bodies. Combined with a weighted centroid identity for the polar body, these estimates yield an explicit $\varepsilon_n>0$ for which the unit ball is the only solution when $-n-\varepsilon_n\le p<-n$.

The key idea is to show that any nontrivial critical point (if it exists) is a nondegenerate global minimum point. Furthermore, we classify the types of all critical points, as well as the splitting phenomena that occur when the number of critical points changes. Applications to Riemann theta functions are also given. In particular, we resolve a conjecture of Luo and Wei (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 2022).

♻ ☆ Strong and weak mean value sets for elliptic operators: uniqueness and counterexamples
Niles Armstrong, Ivan Blank
Classical theorems of Epstein--Schiffer and Kuran characterize balls by the mean value identity for integrable harmonic functions. In the Fermi Lectures, Caffarelli described an obstacle problem construction of analogous averaging sets for symmetric uniformly elliptic divergence-form operators. For such an operator with bounded measurable coefficients in dimension $n \ge 2,$ fix a center $x_0$ and a volume $V > 0,$ and let $E$ be the corresponding canonical set. We prove that a bounded open set $D$ of volume $V$ containing $x_0$ satisfies the mean value inequality at $x_0$ for every integrable subsolution on $D$ if and only if $E \subset D \subset \operatorname{int}\overline{E}.$ In particular, every such strong mean value set agrees with $E$ almost everywhere. The proof uses weak modified Schwarz potentials and an energy comparison. Additionally, we construct smooth symmetric uniformly elliptic operators for which the unit ball satisfies the mean value identity for all integrable solutions but fails the subsolution inequality, showing that there can be two distinct notions for what one can consider to be a ''mean value set.'' The canonical mean value set with the same center and volume contains the entire unit sphere and has a hole of positive measure inside the unit ball.

We construct nonnegative constrained minimizers for nonsingular approximating problems and, under the stated variational and boundary-control hypotheses, obtain a positive normalized weak solution as the reaction regularization vanishes. The approximation preserves the prescribed modular and yields subsequential strong Sobolev convergence of the states together with convergence of their constraint multipliers, while the gradient regularization remains fixed. Finally, we present a normalized singular problem on the unit disk as an illustrative example.
♻ ☆ Existence and uniqueness of solutions of degenerate elliptic equations with lower order terms
Seyma Cetin, David Cruz-Uribe, Feyza Elif Dal, Scott Rodney, Yusuf Zeren
We prove the existence and uniqueness of solutions to a Dirichlet problem \[ \begin{cases} Lu = f + v^{-1}\text{Div}(v{\bf e} h), & x \in Ω; u = 0, & x \in \partial Ω, \end{cases}\] where $L$ is a degenerate, linear, second order elliptic operator with lower order terms. We assume very weak hypotheses, in terms of the coefficients of the equation, and we also assume the existence of degenerate Sobolev and Poincaré inequalities. One notable feature of our result is that we show that we can assume significantly weaker versions of the Sobolev inequality if we in turn assume stronger integrability conditions on the coefficients. Our theorems generalize a number of results in the literature on degenerate elliptic equations.

♻ ☆ Quadrature-Induced Local Minima in Structure-Preserving Lotka-Volterra Control
Alexandre Autran
We study how the choice of harvest quadrature affects optimal control in a positivity-preserving Lotka--Volterra scheme. With harvesting alone, counting the prey removed at each step gives a strictly convex cost. Using the prey density at the start of the step overestimates the catch and can create a strict local minimum with cost above the global minimum. We certify the global minimizers in a two-step example by rational root isolation. A second example shows that, with both species present and positive diffusion, a strict local minimizer for the old-state rule admits a descent direction under the flux rule. For nonnegative $H^1$ initial data and positive diffusivities in one space dimension, the two rules give costs, weighted gradients and Hessians that differ by $O(τ)$ at the same control, uniformly in the spatial mesh. Here $τ$ is the time step. If the old-state Hessian is uniformly coercive near a stationary control, the flux objective has a local minimizer within $O(τ)$ of it. With uniformly bounded tracking targets, a large enough effort penalty makes both objectives strongly convex for all sufficiently small time steps. We also derive exact discrete adjoints and Hessian actions, prove a common variational limit with an IMEX discretization, and compare stationary controls across grids. The same harvest accounting applies to weighted production--destruction systems.

Functional Analysis
☆ A symmetric eigenvalue lower bound for Hadamard products

The proof combines a spectral minorant of $B$ whose diagonal entries are at least $μ_j(B)$ with the projection inequality underlying the companion bound. ☆ Irreducible shallow tanh neural networks are a manifold
Ivan Bioli, Isabella Carla Gonnella, Carlo Marcati, Federico Pichi
Neural networks (NNs) have been increasingly used as function approximators, motivating the study of the geometry of their function spaces. We study the set of functions represented by shallow neural networks with hyperbolic tangent activation, fixed input and output dimensions, and $n$ hidden neurons. In particular, we prove that the subset represented by irreducible networks in the sense of Sussmann (Neural Networks, 1992), i.e., networks with no redundant neurons, is a smooth embedded submanifold of the Sobolev spaces $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ on bounded sets for any $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\in[1,+\infty]$. The key step is to show that if a sequence of networks converges in $\mathrm{W}^{\ell,p}$ to an irreducible network with the same number of hidden neurons, then the parameters of the approximating networks remain bounded. Finally, we show that this manifold has exactly $n+1$ connected components when both the input and output are scalar, and is connected otherwise.

We study when the coefficients of a linearly parameterized analytic system can be identified from a single input-solution pair. Given a finite dictionary of analytic operators, each admissible input induces a finite-dimensional linear recovery map from coefficients to observed outputs. Coefficient recovery is possible exactly when this map is injective. We define the degenerate input set as the set of inputs for which injectivity fails and prove a zero-one law: either every admissible input is degenerate, or the degenerate set is negligible in the sense that it is compactly slice-null and has zero measure under every nondegenerate Gaussian measure. We then apply this framework to the recovery of matrices, analytic continuous-time dynamical systems, and differential operators. For several ODE and PDE classes, we further characterize the degenerate sets explicitly and identify deterministic choices of inputs that guarantee recovery.

We prove a two-sided transfer principle for second-order systems with Hilbert-valued infinite memory. The squared norm of the coupled semigroup, from a centered weighted-history space into the energy space, is bounded above and below by constant multiples of $ρ_w(t)$. Here $ρ_w(t)$ is the squared norm of the right-translation semigroup between the corresponding weighted and unweighted memory spaces. The coupled system satisfies an energy identity, a mechanical multiplier estimate and a bounded observation. The memory density has decay of order at most polynomial, and the weight is admissible. Under these hypotheses the energy is bounded by the initial norm times $κ(t)+ρ_w(t)$, where $κ$ is the tail of the kernel. The two-sided equivalence holds when $ρ_w$ is integrable and the kernel has a finite first moment and satisfies a tail bound, or when $κ\le C_κρ_w$. For the density $pb(1+s)^{-p-1}$, with $p>1$ and $b>0$, and the weight $(1+s)^{2θ}$, with $θ>0$, the rate is $(1+t)^{-\min\{2θ,p+1\}}$. For kernels and weights with logarithmic factors, under explicit conditions on the exponents, the logarithm of the weight enters the rate below the saturation threshold, and the logarithm of the kernel enters above it. A theorem with a prescribed decay of the inherited history gives exact exponents for algebraically growing histories. The hypotheses are verified for gradient-memory waves without instantaneous damping, endpoint-damped strings, damped plates and oscillators.

For scalar targets with disjoint expanding branches that strictly cover their convex hull, this $C^1$ control and parabolic compactness yield compact invariant sets of the exact response. These sets factor onto the full one sided shift and contain periodic densities of every least period. Nondegenerate periodic orbits continue, and hyperbolicity requires a separate strict multiplier condition. We also prove a derivative cost obstruction for nonaffine microscopic realization, a susceptibility weighted criterion for population energy designs, and the failure of exact scalar closure under nontrivial rank one feedback. The results concern designed frozen law responses, not Nash consistent mean field game equilibria or finite player limits.

♻ ☆ The Brown--Shields Conjecture: Two Approximation Theorems and a Counterexample
Bonan Chen, Xiang Fang, Feng Guo
We construct an outer function in the classical Dirichlet space whose radial zero set has logarithmic capacity zero, but whose polynomial multiples do not approximate the constant function $1$. This disproves the Brown--Shields conjecture. The proof rests on two approximation theorems for canonical generators of invariant subspaces. The first shows that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated in the Dirichlet norm by canonical generators associated with singular inner functions determined by finite positive atomic measures. The second shows that each fixed finite-atomic canonical generator can be recovered as a strong Dirichlet limit of outer canonical generators whose radial zero sets have arbitrarily small logarithmic capacity. We then combine these approximations using two techniques: a complete metric that controls boundary logarithms and a nested-ball construction that preserves outerness and noncyclicity while ensuring that the radial zero set is polar. In fact, we show that every proper outer canonical generator can be approximated arbitrarily closely by such counterexamples, both in the Dirichlet norm and in the $L^1$ norm of their boundary logarithms.

The deformed derivative maps the holomorphic functions on a disc of radius $ρ$ into those on the disc of radius $ρ/β$, $β$ being the upper limit of the $n-$th roots of the deformed numbers, and this loss of radius is optimal. For two root structure functions the deformed gauge equals $\max\{|z|,1/φ_{1}\}$, so that deformed discs are Euclidean above a minimal radius; Borel Carathéodory and vector valued Cauchy Hadamard theorems follow. On factorial weighted Banach spaces the deformed derivative has norm $1/r$ and spectrum the closed disc of radius $1/r$. A deformed Borel transform identifies these spaces with weighted Wiener algebras, yields the Gelfand theory, and shows that the associated Fréchet space is nuclear. We establish logarithmic convexity and subharmonicity results, Phragmén Lindelöf and Lindelöf principles in the anisotropic sectors of half aperture $θ\sup_{k}k^{-1}\log[k]$ and in their curved variants, with sharp critical orders, and a rigidity theorem: under Gaussian growth of the deformed factorials, functions of finite deformed exponential type are entire of order zero and cannot be bounded on a ray unless constant. A dominant term principle shows that, for a large dominant root, the deformed exponential and trigonometric functions have only real simple zeros, localized between explicit geometric means of deformed numbers, whereas the deformed exponential series has nonreal zeros when the two roots have sum at most two.

♻ ☆ Local-to-Global Isometries in Standard-Norm Generalized Gyrovector Spaces
Osamu Hatori
Every bijective gyrometric isometry between nonempty connected open subsets of simply connected generalized gyrovector spaces (GGVs) with real value-line structure extends uniquely to a global bijective isometry. The extension is a left gyrotranslation composed with an isometry preserving the identity, gyroaddition, and scalar multiplication. Gyromidpoints and point reflections give continuation of local isometry germs. Without assuming simple connectedness, a global bijective isometric extension exists exactly when the germs of the map and its inverse are fixed by their respective monodromy actions. Continuity of each fixed-scalar multiplication map implies contractibility and hence simple connectedness. We construct standard-norm GGVs for $t>0$ on positive invertible cones of nonzero unital JB-algebras and, in dimension greater than one, on their projective cones. Power maps relate their gyrometrics to Thompson's and Hilbert's metrics, respectively, with equality at $t=1$. Thus for both metrics, bijective isometries between nonempty connected open subsets extend uniquely to global bijective isometries. We give proofs of the known Thompson and Hilbert isometry classifications, together with their power-coordinate forms for every $t>0$, using the GGV Mazur--Ulam theorem and recovering the Jordan structures from infinitesimal gyrations. Applications include a new proof of Mankiewicz's theorem on connected open subsets of real normed spaces and a local extension theorem for hyperbolic balls in real inner product spaces, including incomplete and infinite-dimensional spaces. We also give constructions for products and function spaces.

We study target suboptimality for points that approximately minimize a surrogate objective. Unlike standard uniform perturbation estimates, the available comparison is one-sided, thresholded at a certified lower target level, and restricted to the entire surrogate-selected sublevel set. We first show that selected comparison alone cannot yield a finite worst-case guarantee, even for strongly convex quadratics with identical Hessians. A single scalar upper bound on the surrogate minimum closes this information gap and leads to a sharp general estimate. For pairs of $μ$-strongly convex and $L$-smooth objectives, we then solve the associated worst-case information problem exactly. We obtain a sharp feasibility barrier and a dimension-free envelope; in its nontrivial regime, the value reduces to a scalar maximization over a compact interval. Explicit one-dimensional piecewise-quadratic objectives attain the bound while satisfying the one-sided constraint on the full selected set. We characterize when curvature strictly improves the general certificate and provide a threshold-preserving finite-net validation procedure. The results identify the best guarantee permitted by the prescribed partial information, independently of any particular optimization algorithm or additive perturbation model.

For one convex curve in each plane this recovers, by a different method, the nonexistence and rigidity theorem of Bernstein and Breiner. The bound extends to non-convex curves and to boundaries with several components. Finally, we show that the Meeks annulus conjecture is equivalent to the absence of atoms in the area functions of the hulls of all intermediate sections.

When $V=0$ and the nonlinearity is defocusing or sufficiently weakly focusing, adding two explicit control potentials of finite regularity gives local exact controllability in $H^2$ near the constant state, via a moment problem and the inverse mapping theorem. Together, these results imply global exact controllability in $H^2$ on the unit sphere of $L^2$, at any prescribed positive time, with five control potentials. To~the best of our knowledge, this is the first global exact controllability result for a nonlinear Schrödinger equation with finitely many bilinear controls.

For even weights, an odd Morse index of at least $k$ on the principal symmetric component forces at least $k$ symmetry-breaking points. In particular, symmetry breaking occurs if $a(0)<0$.

We also establish sharp moment inequalities and tightness criteria for the radial pole trace and boundary slope. At the sharp fractional $L^p$ Hardy coefficient, we identify the pole flux in a nonlinear power balance and show that finite remainder excludes nonconstant strong angular traces. For every fractional order, positive data can have finite remainder but infinite source pairing. Finally, for singular heat reactions with a positive nonincreasing factor tending to zero at infinity, we determine all attainable reaction limits of a time impulse and of data exhausted by parabolic Kato measures. A total variation estimate describes the combination of these mechanisms for countably many impulses.

This revision corrects the axis reduction of earlier versions and replaces the $(1+1)$-dimensional systems studied there. On the axes the angular pressure terms produce $P_{θθ}$, which we close by $x^{-2}P_{θθ}=-f\,P_{xx}$; consistency at the apex $x=0$ forces $f(t,0)\in\{0,2\}$, and we take $f\equiv2$. Hence, in explicit parameter windows, smooth compactly supported finite-energy data lose smoothness no later than $T_{\rm apex}$ while $E_m$ stays finite. A self-similar analysis describes the inner layer at the apex; for $(R2)$ in its window, computations show blow-up at the apex at $T_{\rm apex}$ with bounded energy, and the residual gap is explained by a short-wave instability seeded by rounding errors. No ratio $b/a$ gives both rays generically finite energy. Finally, with two closure functions the reduction is exact, the apex dynamics contains one free function, the anisotropy of the pressure Hessian at the origin, and we prove that keeping it in an explicit window forces finite-time blow-up of $(E1)$ and $(E2)$ themselves.

♻ ☆ Short-wave signal versus indirect prey-taxis
Andrey Morgulis, Karrar Malal
We address short-wave asymptotics for one class of quasi-linear second-order PDE systems involving the cross-diffusion described by the so-called Patlak-Keller-Segel law. It is common to employ these equations for modeling the predator-prey community with the prey-taxis, which means the interactions of two species of particles or cells through which the species called "predators" is capable of moving directionally while searching for the other species called "prey." However, we suppose the predators to be sensitive not to the prey density but to a cue produced by the prey. Additionally, the production of the cue is assumed to be sensitive to the intensity of an external field, which is independent of the community state. This is what we call the external signal. It can be due to the spatiotemporal inhomogeneity of the environment arising from natural or artificial reasons. We assume that the external signal takes a general short-wave form and construct a complete formal asymptotic expansion for the short-wave solutions (modulo solving a chain of the so-called slow systems) with no restrictions on the spatial dimension or kinetics of inter- or intra-specific reactions. Further, we apply the short-wave asymptotic to studying the stability or instability induced by the external signal following Kapitza's theory for the upside-down pendulum. Applying the general results to some special classes of external signals, we get examples of suppressing the taxical transport, examples of the robustness of the species equilibrium to the signal up to a very strong stabilization or, oppositely, destabilization and blurring the borderline in the parametric space between the areas of stability and instability of this equilibrium.

☆ Shadow economy as a null set. Measure-theoretic approach to shadow economy
Radosław A. Kycia, Andrzej Buszko
In this paper we asked if the shadow economy can be defined as a system of null sets for institutional measures or sensors that measure economic transactions. As an answer a measure-theoretic testable framework to redefine and quantify the shadow economy was designed. Traditional economic definitions frequently conflate the actual shadow economy with the observational limitations of state institutions. To resolve this, we model the shadow economy as a null set relative to institutional measures and analyze three complementary economic regimes. We explore in this context how standard mathematical tools can be given economic meaning. First, in the low-resolution regime, we apply Banach Lattices and Lebesgue decomposition of a measure to address transaction underreporting by aggregating incomplete institutional registries using a supremum fusion operator. Second, for hidden economic dimensions, we utilize Copula theory and Kullback-Leibler divergence optimization to reconstruct unobserved financial flows from technological and physical indicators. Third, we address audit scalability by modeling the shadow economy as a sparse vector, applying Compressed Sensing to detect high-volume sparse evasion networks through random, incoherent, and privacy-preserving sampling.

While the former enjoys well-known $L^p$--$L^q$ estimates, the latter may fail to satisfy any such bounds without additional assumptions; nevertheless, weaker forms of boundedness can still be recovered under suitable conditions. The representation formula is intended as a tool for the study of Schatten-type properties of commutators $[b,T]$ of fractional integrals and pointwise multipliers, which will be addressed in a forthcoming companion work by T. Hytönen and the author. Beyond this application, the representation itself may be of independent interest and useful in other contexts.
☆ Decomposition of completeness and the universality of the Daniell extension
Hayato Saito
An integration system is a triple $(X,L,I)$: a set $X$, a Riesz subspace $L$ of $\mathbb{R}^X$, and a continuous positive linear functional $I$ on $L$. We introduce the category Int whose morphisms are pullbacks along maps of the base spaces. The main result is that the Daniell extension defines a functor from Int to DInt and is left adjoint to the inclusion of the full subcategory DInt of Daniell closed systems, those with $L^1=L$, usually called complete. So DInt is reflective and the Daniell extension is its reflector. The content lies in a decomposition: a system is Daniell closed if and only if it satisfies the monotone convergence theorem and is closed under modification on null sets, and neither can be dropped. The second corresponds to completeness of the measure. The decomposition is a real-valued phenomenon: for extended-real-valued functions the second condition follows from the first. Daniell closedness of the codomain cannot be omitted. The inclusion of the category of systems satisfying the monotone convergence theorem also has a left adjoint, but its reflector is not the Daniell extension. Under the Stone condition that second reflection consists of the integrable functions measurable for the $σ$-algebra generated by $L$. For an arbitrary system, $L^1$ splits as the sum of that part and the functions supported on null sets, so the gap between the two reflections is exactly the completion of the measure. Finally, if morphisms are replaced by positive linear maps between Riesz spaces, they see only the quotient of $L$ by the null functions, where the Daniell extension gives the Banach completion. So the distinction between an abstract completion and a concrete realization survives as categorical structure only where morphisms are maps of base spaces. In sum: the Daniell counterpart of the completion of a measure space, in categorical language.

A. V. Utkin
This paper develops Chernoff-type approximation methods for strongly continuous and bi-continuous semigroups of operators arising in the stochastic dynamics of quantum systems. The main focus is on applying Chernoff iterations to Markov semigroups of multiplicative random processes on separable infinite-dimensional Hilbert spaces. The justification of the passage from discrete quantum measurements to continuous ones depends essentially on the choice of topology and function spaces. We propose conditions for convergence to bi-continuous semigroups on subspaces that weaken the classical requirements of the Chernoff theorem. The existence of the limiting bi-continuous semigroup is established in each of the three cases: commutation of the approximating operators, their asymptotic commutation, and uniform convergence of difference quotients over a family of approximating operators. For diffusive models with a generator having bounded coefficients, the derivative of the approximating function is computed explicitly on the subspace of test functions with rapidly decreasing second derivative; the limitations of applicability of this result are discussed. Applications to generalized models of continuous imprecise quantum measurement with unbounded observables, as well as to Poisson and diffusion processes, are outlined as directions for further research.

In this paper, we introduce and study the directional short-time special affine Fourier transform (DSTSAFT) in the multidimensional setting. Motivated by the need to combine localized time-frequency analysis with directional sensitivity and the flexibility of the special affine Fourier transform, the DSTSAFT provides a unified framework that encompasses established directional transforms as particular cases. Furthermore, we prove that both the DSTSAFT and its synthesis operator are continuous mappings between the corresponding spaces of test functions. Building on these continuity results, we extend the DSTSAFT and its synthesis operator to the corresponding spaces of tempered distributions via duality. We also establish an important relationship between the DSTSAFT and the special affine Fourier transform (SAFT) and derive a desingularization formula. The resulting framework provides an analytical basis for studying directional and localized properties of tempered distributions within the SAFT setting.

Without assuming cyclicity, we give a weak compactness criterion and local variation conditions for reflexive dilations; an example on $\ell_2$ shows that reflexivity alone is insufficient. For a separable space containing no $c_0$, a normalized operator-valued measure is induced by a continuous Schauder frame if and only if it admits a cyclic dilation and has $σ$-finite operator-norm variation. Finally, for measure quotients whose synthesis maps admit bounded linear right inverses, we construct compatible cyclic $L_p$-dilations and represent the quotient spaces as inductive limits, with applications to ReLU Barron spaces.

Let $\mathcal{H}_{i}$ be complex separable Hilbert spaces and $T_{i}\in\mathcal{B}(\mathcal{H}_{i})$ for $i=1,\dots,n$. We deduce from some results in the literature that $\mathbf{DVL}$ and $\mathbf{UVL}$ are reflective subcategories of $\mathbf{DAOVS}$, with the usual Dedekind completion being the reflector in $\mathbf{DVL}$. Third, we show that the $α$-power generalization of the Hornich-Hlawka inequality fails to hold on nonzero normed spaces when $α\in (1, 2) \cup (2, \infty)$. For the remaining two problems, we establish reductions. We prove that $\ell^p(N)$ is Hornich-Hlawka for all $N \geq 3$ and $2 < p \leq \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$ if and only if it is Hornich-Hlawka at $N = 3$ and $p = \log 3 /(\log 3 - \log 2)$.
