Within the single-particle continuum model, the invariant of an $m$-layer stack equals the difference of occupied angular weights of the zero-momentum levels, which reduces the classification to the ordering of those levels. At equal coupling, nonlinear monotone potentials reproduce exactly the set of invariants of linear potentials, also under the requirement of a common energy gap: screening moves phase boundaries but creates no new invariant values. With bond-dependent coupling, we characterize all occupied configurations. The range of attainable invariants is unchanged, but the gaps inside it are filled, beginning at five layers. Reflection-symmetric stacks realize a large subfamily with a guaranteed common gap, and lower bounds on single-bulk gaps complete the set of invariants with a common global gap for five and six layers. Among the examples is an eight-layer domain wall defined purely by gates, whose number of co-propagating channels per valley switches from 8 to 16 as the gate strength increases. Exact transfer-matrix calculations of the interface spectrum reproduce every predicted signed crossing count. A norm bound gives the minimum spread of interlayer coupling compatible with a prescribed gap.

The separating maps form a family of radial damping maps $T(x)=λ(\norm{x})x$ on a normed space, where $λ\colon[0,\infty)\to[0,ρ]$ is continuous, $0\leρ<1$, nonconstant and periodic: every such map is a relaxed asymptotic contraction with explicit linear moduli, whereas its one-step dispersion at a fixed distance is unbounded, so that no finite Kirk modulus exists. We also extend the analysis to state-dependent terms that may be singular near the boundary and obtain sharp boundary profiles and gradient asymptotics. Our approach relies on stochastic optimal control and boundary blow-up analysis. Dynamic programming estimates and comparisons of near-optimal trajectories establish tangential invariance of boundary blow-up limits, leading to the identification of one-dimensional profiles and the asymptotic formulas. For the associated state-constrained control problem, we establish sharp asymptotics for the minimizing feedback and deduce its admissibility and optimality, with corresponding results for the ergodic problem.

The conformable derivative defines a local change of time coordinate, while exchange with immobile regions supplies the memory. Positive Gauss--Jacobi quadrature approximates the prescribed exchange spectrum by finite compartments. Both schemes use conservative finite-volume fluxes. Forward Euler gives the explicit update; backward Euler initializes the implicit second-order backward differentiation formula (BDF2). Eliminating the compartment states reduces each implicit step to a tridiagonal system. Under stated mesh and regularity conditions, we prove implicit solvability, conditional explicit positivity and stability, and discrete mass balance. A cell-average error estimate separates spatial, compartment and temporal contributions. Its proof accounts for the boundary fluxes and the BDF2 startup error. Source-specific bounds make the temporal and memory prefactors uniform under mesh and compartment refinement. For a broader positive-history model, continuous residual estimates have coefficients independent of memory strength and kernel mass. Local coercivity gives a sharper coefficient. Manufactured tests recover second-order spatial convergence, first-order Euler convergence and second-order BDF2 convergence. Separate experiments examine the memory and combined estimates. In a prescribed porous-medium application, the finest numerical states differ by $3.57\times10^{-5}$ in relative space--time $L^2$. Independent resolution checks support the computed pulse attenuation, immobile storage and release after injection ends.

In the second-order nonlocal term, we write $g$ as the sum of its velocity mollification and a remainder. Uniform continuity makes the remainder small. For the mollified part, two integrations by parts give a bound proportional to the length of the time interval.

The shear and second viscosities have a common density exponent between one half and one, inclusive. Throughout the strictly dissipative range of viscosity coefficients, every pressure exponent greater than or equal to one is admissible. In particular, the result applies to Marche's viscous shallow water equations on a flat bottom in the absence of rotation, bottom friction, and capillarity. These equations retain the positive second viscosity derived from free-surface flow and thus fall outside the Bresch-Desjardins relation. The density stays bounded above and away from zero uniformly in time. On the disk, the density converges exponentially to its spatial mean and the velocity to zero in the Sobolev norm of order three. In the plane, convergence in the same norm holds to the prescribed far-field state. The argument also applies to a class of non-power viscosity laws.

♻ ☆ Finite speed Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac processes and their applications in generative modeling
Richard Duong, Janis Auffenberg, Gabriele Steidl
We study the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-Kac (OU-K) process, where instead of a Brownian motion, a finite-speed Kac process defines the driving process. The OU-K process can be analyzed through a rescaled, time-inhomogeneous Kac process, characterized by a switching rate from the Kac part, and a convergence rate from the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck (OU) part. The law of this inhomogeneous Kac process describes the solution of a wave equation, the Euler-Poisson-Darboux (EPD) equation. For Kac switching rates being multiples of the OU convergence rate, we can explicitly derive this EPD solution via the sum of (the derivative of) two Legendre polynomials, restricted between two Dirac points representing the wave fronts. Using the framework of piecewise-deterministic Markov processes (PDMP), we describe the conditional velocity fields of the OU-K process via our polynomial-law-formula. This allows us to apply the OU-K process in a generative flow model. Since the OU-K velocity fields prove to be bounded by the finite Kac speed, the usual time truncations of diffusion models become unnecessary. We demonstrate advantages over diffusion and flow matching models in terms of generation sharpness on singular data sets, while achieving competitive results on CIFAR-10 image generation.

As plasticity is modeled through a non-smooth dissipation potential, we introduce a weak formulation in terms of a variational inequality. Since the well-posedness in such a weak setting is out of reach, we study two possible modifications: the regularization in terms of stress diffusion, and the relaxation of the solvability concept by transition to energy-variational solutions. In both cases, solutions are constructed by the same time-discrete scheme, consisting of solving a saddle-point problem in each time step.

Environmental DNA (eDNA) is increasingly used to monitor aquatic organisms in rivers, yet predicting its concentration and assessing the reliability of such predictions remain challenging because river flow fluctuates with long memory and models of eDNA dynamics are inevitably misspecified. We propose a stochastic modeling framework for eDNA concentration in rivers that addresses both issues. The eDNA concentration is described by a stochastic partial differential equation with transport, decay, source, and square-root multiplicative noise, and the flow velocity is modeled by a superposition of Ornstein-Uhlenbeck-type processes with long memory. We show that the long memory of the flow velocity induces superdiffusive transport of eDNA, with the variance of the transported distance growing superlinearly in the ensemble sense. The proposed model admits a closed-form Laplace functional, based on which we prove the existence and uniqueness in law of the solution on an unbounded domain. We further evaluate the effects of model uncertainty through a robust control formulation based on the relative entropy, in which the lower and upper bounds of the expected eDNA concentration, together with the worst-case distortions, are obtained in closed form. The framework is applied to eDNA and flow velocity data collected for the upstream migration of Plecoglossus altivelis altivelis in a river in Japan. The results demonstrate that the closed-form bounds provide a computationally inexpensive tool for quantifying the range of eDNA concentrations that can be expected under model uncertainty.

For a general class of uniformly superlinear integrands satisfying a $Δ_2$-condition, we establish existence and uniqueness of minimizers and derive a Fenchel dual problem with dual attainment and pointwise optimality conditions. We then specialize the framework to a logarithmic density whose correction is activated above a prescribed local gradient scale. For this model, we obtain explicit expressions of the Fenchel dual and optimality conditions as well as a pointwise radial formula for the dual proximal map involving the Lambert $W$-function. As the logarithmic parameter tends to zero, we prove equicoercivity and $Γ$-convergence to the ROF functional, together with convergence of the corresponding minimizers. Numerical illustrations indicate that the logarithmic correction can reduce staircasing for diffuse transitions, while retaining behavior comparable to ROF for sharp interfaces and a natural image.

Photoacoustic tomography is an emerging medical imaging technology whose primary aim is to map the high-contrast optical properties of biological tissues by leveraging high-resolution ultrasound measurements. Mathematically, this can be framed as an inverse source problem for the wave equation over a specific domain. In this work, for the first time, it is shown how, by assuming signal sparsity, it is possible to establish rigorous stable recovery guarantees when the data collection is given by spatial averages restricted to a sparse, randomly sampled portion of the boundary. Our framework encompasses many approaches that have been considered in the literature. The result is a consequence of a general framework for subsampled inverse problems developed in previous works and refined stability estimates for an inverse problem for the wave equation with surface measurements.

♻ ☆ Existence and partial regularity of suitable weak solutions to the 3D Navier-Stokes-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equations
Renjun Duan, Fengqiang Shi, Wendong Wang, Jianbo Yu
In this paper, we investigate the incompressible Navier-Stokes equations coupled with the Vlasov-Fokker-Planck equation, which describes a two-phase mixture of the viscous incompressible fluid with particles or bubbles through a frictional force term. In the three-dimensional whole space, we construct a new class of suitable weak solutions to the Navier-Stokes-Vlasov-Fokker-Planck system satisfying energy estimates and three local or global energy inequalities of different forms. These obtained local energy inequalities play an important role in characterizing the measure of the singularity set of weak solutions. The main difficulties in deriving these inequalities lie in establishing the convergence of the density function $f$ in bounded or unbounded domains and dealing with the convergence of the non-local frictional force term. The strong $L^1$ convergence of $|v|^k f$ for $0\le k<κ$ and of $|v|^k f\log f$ locally in $x$ for $0\le k<κ/2$ is proved by using new a priori estimates for the velocity, Tao's $L^p$ decomposition, and the DiPerna-Lions compactness method. Moreover, as an immediate consequence of the existence result, we are able to describe the Hausdorff dimension of set of singular points of the fluid velocity $u$ and also establish the $α$-Hölder continuity of $f$ at the regular points of $u$.
♻ ☆ Global Regularity for the Chemotaxis-Stokes System with Signal Consumption in $\mathbb{R}^3$
Fengqiang Shi, Wendong Wang, Guoxu Yang
Motivated by the continuum model of aerobic bacteria proposed by Tuval et al. in 2005, we study the large-data regularity problem for the three-dimensional chemotaxis--Stokes system with signal consumption. We prove the global existence and uniqueness of classical solutions to the Cauchy problem in $\mathbb R^3$ for smooth initial data with finite density mass and moment and finite signal Fisher information, without any smallness assumptions. The proof is based on three main ideas. First, we use a terminal heat-kernel representation to define a finite signal value at every spatial point and prove strong $L^a$ convergence of the backward parabolic signal rescalings to this value for every $1\le a<\infty$. Second, we prove a localized entropy estimate that remains uniform under density normalization, even when the resulting consumption coefficient becomes arbitrarily large. These estimates give two complementary mechanisms: consumption excludes normalized density concentration at points with positive terminal signal, while a localized weighted estimate improves density integrability at points with zero terminal signal. Third, we establish a local $\varepsilon$-regularity criterion based on smallness of scale-invariant density, velocity, and pressure quantities. A heat decomposition recovers the required signal-gradient smallness, removing it as a separate assumption. Together, these yield the decay of a scale-invariant density quantity and then exclude finite-time singularities.

♻ ☆ Decoupling and Tail Laws for Small-Order Metric-Valued Nonlocal Energies: A Structural View of the Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova Formula
Andrea Pinamonti
We develop a measure-theoretic framework for small-order limits of nonlocal energies with metric-valued maps. For globally $L^p$ maps, we consider interaction measures whose marginals have uniformly bounded $L^\infty$ densities $a_α$ and $b_α$. If these densities converge weakly-* to $a_\infty$ and $b_\infty$, the normalized energies converge to the $L^p$ energy weighted by $a_\infty+b_\infty$ if and only if the interaction measures escape every bounded rectangle. For maps that are only locally $L^p$, we introduce target laws describing the distribution of the values sampled at infinity. Convergence of their $p$-distance profiles yields the limiting interaction energy for every $1\leq p<\infty$ and arbitrary Polish targets, with integrated $p$-Wasserstein convergence as a sufficient criterion. The arguments include the endpoint $p=1$ and require no linear structure on the target space. Applications include directional and anisotropic Maz'ya--Shaposhnikova formulas, a Bernoulli-law interpretation of fractional perimeters, and an Abelian principle for heat-semigroup energies.
♻ ☆ Global renormalized finite-energy weak solutions to the three-dimensional compressible Navier-Stokes system on tori for $γ>4/3$
Guangyi Hong, Hongyun Peng, Changjiang Zhu
Building on the foundational theory of finite-energy weak solutions initiated by P.-L. Lions and further developed by E. Feireisl and collaborators, we establish the global existence of finite-energy renormalized weak solutions to the compressible Navier--Stokes equations on the three-dimensional torus, with constant viscosity coefficients and pressure law \(P(ρ)=ρ^γ\), for every \(γ>4/3\) and arbitrary finite-energy initial data. This extends the classical three-dimensional Lions--Feireisl existence theory beyond the threshold \(γ>3/2\), and in particular, covers the important case $ γ=7/5 $ for air (cf. \cite{Anderson}). Compared to the classical theory, we develop a novel approach to establish the improved pressure-integrability estimate compatible with the viscous and inertial terms, via constructing a periodic test field through barycentric optimal transport. This improved pressure-integrability estimate, combined with an effective viscous flux identity and an entropy comparison, provides the compactness needed to identify the nonlinear limits and recover the energy inequality.

♻ ☆ Liouville systems I: Blow-up analysis and orthogonal decomposition
Mohameden Ahmedou, Jonas Fey, Zhengni Hu, Lei Zhang
We study blow-up solutions of generalized Liouville systems on a closed surface at and near critical parameter hypersurfaces. Under a Morse assumption on the reduced functional, we establish the following results. First, we introduce amplitude variables in the approximate manifold and prove that every sequence of blow-up solutions at a fixed critical parameter, or along an admissible sequence from the lower side, admits a unique minimizing decomposition up to permutation. The remainder converges to zero and is orthogonal to the center, scale, and amplitude directions. The concentration scales are comparable, the limiting configuration satisfies the scale balance conditions, and the amplitudes vanish after multiplication by the logarithmic scale. Second, we determine the leading parameter defect in both critical decay regimes and prove that, along each fixed admissible path, all sufficiently large solutions lie in finitely many disjoint bubbling neighborhoods. Finally, assuming the leading coefficient is nonzero at every balanced critical configuration, the solution set at the fixed critical parameter is compact. These results provide the analytic foundation for studying the resonant degree via critical points at infinity.

♻ ☆ Existence of weak solutions of the surface Beris-Edwards model
Gonzalo A. Benavides, Ricardo H. Nochetto, Mansur Shakipov
We prove the existence of weak solutions to the surface Beris-Edwards model for nematic liquid crystals posed on a $d$-dimensional ($d \in \{2,3\}$) closed hypersurface of class $C^{2,1}$. This thermodynamically consistent model, recently introduced by Bouck, Nochetto and Yushutin (2024), couples the incompressible tangent Navier-Stokes equations with a kinematic equation for the Q-tensor field that encodes the orientation of the liquid crystal particles with a general state of orientational order. Extending ideas by Abels, Dolzmann and Liu (2014) and Guillén-González and Rodríguez-Bellido (2015) for the Beris-Edwards model in flat domains, we design a Faedo-Galerkin scheme based upon eigenfunctions of an appropriate tangent Stokes operator and tensor-valued Laplace-Beltrami operator and recover a weak solution via standard compactness arguments.

♻ ☆ Numerical reconstruction of polygonal obstacles by diffracted waves
Xi Chen, Kuangmiao Xiong, Boxi Xu
We present a numerical method for recovering rigid polygonal obstacles in two dimensions, based on the diffraction-based inverse scattering theory of Bao, Chen, Lu, and Xiong. A single pulse is emitted from a point source, and the resulting wave field is measured on a receiver curve. After isolating the diffracted signals, we recover the visible vertices from arrival times and the corner orientations and opening angles from amplitudes. The use of amplitude information permits local reconstruction in the reflection shadow, where reflected waves do not reach the receiver. The amplitudes also determine the direction of a shadowed edge adjacent to a visible vertex, enabling local non-line-of-sight imaging. Numerical experiments for a convex corner, a concave corner, a triangle, a pentagon, and a star-shaped obstacle confirm that the visible portion of the boundary can be recovered stably from diffracted signals. A further convex-corner test with additive noise at level $0.2\%$ on the single arc $L_{1}$ confirms that the tip and opening remain recoverable.
comment: 20 pages, 21 figures
♻ ☆ An indefinite Coulomb interaction from the Steklov spectrum of perforated manifolds
Zhonggan Huang, Raghavendra Venkatraman
We establish optimal convergence rates for Steklov eigenvalues and harmonically extended eigenfunctions toward their weighted Laplace--Beltrami counterparts on a closed manifold perforated by many small geodesic balls. The holes have radii that scale critically with respect to their spacing in the sense that the boundary area of each hole balances with the weighted volume of its Voronoi cell. We then derive a higher-order expansion of the Steklov eigenvalues; in dimensions two and three, we identify two correction scales. The expansion is governed by an indefinite Coulomb-type energy of the discrepancy between the boundary and bulk measures, mediated by the reduced Green function of the limiting operator. The proof relies on sharp estimates for certain auxiliary functions that we introduce in order to quantify the discrepancy measure between the surface measure on the holes and their background density. Our paper serves to bridge an emerging literature in spectral geometry with one on systems of points interacting via Coulomb-type energies.
comment: Minor errors fixed
♻ ☆ Small scale quantum ergodicity in cat maps
Xiaolong Han
We study small scale quantum ergodicity in quantum cat maps, with semiclassical parameter 1/N, and prove three groups of results. First, for every N and every eigenbasis, almost all eigenstates are equidistributed on phase space balls of radius (log N)^(-a) for a<1/2, and on position space balls for a<1. For a set of N of full density and for Hecke eigenbases, almost all eigenstates, and even all of them, are equidistributed at polynomial scales. Second, every invariant probability measure is the semiclassical measure of quasimodes of order 1/log N, one for each N, that are not equidistributed at any scale between 4N^(-1/8) and a prescribed scale tending to zero. Third, there are orthonormal bases of quasimodes of order 1/log N for every N, and eigenbases for N with short periods, in which a full density subset is equidistributed at every fixed scale, but not at the scales (log N)^(-a) for a>1/2 in phase space and a>1 in position space. Hence, the exponents 1/2 and 1 in the first group are sharp: even for a full density subset of eigenstates, quantum ergodicity at fixed scales does not extend beyond the critical logarithmic scales.

Functional Analysis
☆ Weighted sum commuting maps with the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform
Jing-Bin Zhou, Shihai Yang
Let $\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ denote the algebra of all $n\times n$ complex matrices, where $n\geq2$, and let $Δ_{f,g}$ be the $(f,g)$-Aluthge transform associated with nonnegative continuous functions $f,g$ on $[0,\infty)$ satisfying $f(t)g(t)=t$ for all $t\geq0$. In this paper, we characterize all surjective maps $Φ:\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C}) \to\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfying\[Φ(Δ_{f,g}(αA+βB))=Δ_{f,g}(αΦ(A)+βΦ(B))\]for all $A,B\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$, where $α,β$ are fixed nonzero real numbers. Without assuming additivity or linearity, we prove that when $f$ is nonconstant, $Φ$ must be of the form $Φ(A)=cUAU^*$ or $Φ(A)=cU\overline{A}U^*$ for all $A$, where $U$ is a fixed unitary matrix, $\overline{A}$ denotes the entrywise complex conjugate of $A$, and $c$ is a nonzero complex scalar. Moreover, we completely determine the possible values of $|c|$, which form either $\{1\}$, $q^{\mathbb{Z}}$ for some $q>1$, or $(0,\infty)$. When $f$ is constant, we show that $Φ(A)=S(A)+D$ for all $A$, where $S$ is a surjective $\mathbb{Q}(α,β)$-linear map and $D\in\mathbb{M}_n(\mathbb{C})$ satisfies $(α+β-1)D=0$.
☆ Freedom is all you need
Julian Bushelli, James Eldred Pascoe
The functional calculus allows for the rigorous analysis of functions of matrices or even operators. The free functional calculus gives the natural class of functions over any category. We initiate the representation theory for taking a generic free functional calculus to the classical nc functional calculus going back to Taylor, Voiculescu and many others, with an eye towards learning of categories. The functional calculus on direct sum closed and locally similarity (i.e. change of coordinates) invariant domains inherits the niceties of complex analysis and large-scale parallel networks, such as automatic analyticity, free universal monodromy, which gives a hypothetical explanation for beneficial overfitting.
comment: 26 pages. This manuscript was developed, produced, and edited entirely by humans
☆ One exponential or two? Invertibility tests for Jordan epimorphisms
Catalin Badea
How many exponential factors must one test to recognise a Jordan epimorphism? Let \(T\colon A\to B\) be a unital linear surjection between complex Banach algebras, with \(B\) semisimple. Using a spectral-isometry theorem of Aznay and Chabbabi, we show that it suffices for \(T\) to send every product of two exponentials to an invertible element to force $T$ to be Jordan. If only single exponentials are tested, \(T\) is a Jordan epimorphism if and only if its kernel is a two-sided ideal, or equivalently a left ideal. A resolvent estimate on a logarithmic spiral shows that a single exponential suffices when the source is a \(C^*\)-algebra or the group algebra \(\ell^1(G)\) of a discrete group. A separate argument, which does not use the spectral-isometry theorem, shows that a single exponential also suffices when the target is a \(C^*\)-algebra with a faithful family of tracial states.
comment: 16 pages; v1
☆ $L^1$ stability of the entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$ without moment assumptions
Norman El Fartass, Lampros Gavalakis, Ioannis Kontoyiannis
We establish qualitative stability in $L^1$ and Ruzsa distance for Shannon's entropy power inequality in $\mathbb{R}^d$, without any moment assumptions. The proof uses the optimal transport argument by Rioul (2017), majorization bounds of density rearrangements, and the stability of the sharp form of Young's inequality due to Christ (2019). Along the way we also extend recent one-dimensional results on de Bruijn's identity, the continuity of differential entropy, and the equality case of the entropy power inequality to random vectors of any dimension.

☆ Essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees
Lei Liu, Wanxin Ma
We establish characterizations of the essential norms of composition operators on Hardy spaces of homogeneous rooted trees. As direct applications of our main results, we obtain compactness criteria for such composition operators.
☆ Operative Representation of Quasi-Arithmetic Means, Complex Branch Structure, and Covariant Commutator Defects in Iterated Logarithmic Operation Hierarchies
Uwe Heiber
We investigate the bidirectional family of commutative binary operations $\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[x,y] = f_a^{(-m)}(f_a^{(m)}(x) + f_a^{(m)}(y))$ ($m \in \mathbb{Z}$) generated by iterating the scaled logarithmic Cauchy isomorphism $f_a(z) = \frac{1}{a}\ln(z)$ ($a > 0$). Our analysis focuses on three structural properties of this hierarchy. First, we show that for all $m \ge -1$ the associated quasi-arithmetic Kolmogorov-Nagumo means $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x})$ admit a closed two-stage operative representation $S_{\mathrm{Op}_m}(\mathbf{x}) = \mathrm{Op}_{m+1}^{(a)}[\mathrm{Op}_m^{(a)}[\mathbf{x}], N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n)]$ with normalization factor $N_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(n) = f_a^{(-m)}(1/n)$, and prove that this internal operative normalizability via a distributive adjacent level characterizes logarithmic generators among continuously conjugated group operations. Second, we show that for $m \le -2$ and $n \ge 2$ the normalization factor leaves the positive real domain $\mathbb{R}_{>0}$, motivating the analytic continuation onto the Riemann surface of the logarithm; there, a fundamental dichotomy emerges between the internal branch-index invariance of $\mathrm{Op}_{-1}^{(a)}$ and the associativity defect $ω(x,z)$ generated by $\mathrm{Op}_2^{(a)}$. Third, for arbitrary levels $m \in \mathbb{Z}$ and sample sizes $n \in \mathbb{N}$, we derive the general covariance pushforward theorem $\mathrm{Sp}_{\mathrm{Op}_{m+1}}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{y}) = f_a^{(-m)}(\mathrm{Cov}(f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{x}), f_a^{(m)}(\mathbf{y})))$ governing the commutator defect between mean formation and the adjacent operation.
☆ The Garnett--Jones distance theorem for rectangles
Morten Nielsen, Hrvoje Sikic
For the family of all axis-parallel rectangles in $\mathbb R^d$, $d>1$, we characterize the distance of a real- or complex-valued function of rectangular bounded mean oscillation (little bmo) to $L^\infty$ by the reciprocal of its critical exponential integrability exponent. For each $α>0$ at which the rectangular exponential moment of $f$ is finite, we construct a bounded correction so that the residual has mean absolute oscillation bounded by a dimension-dependent constant times $1/α$ on every rectangle. The proof bounds products of coordinate maximal operators between two sets in terms of the supremum of their density product over common test rectangles. Selecting a longest interval along each path lets us remove repeated visits to a coordinate, so the density exponent is independent of the number of factors. The maximal-operator estimate holds with every positive density exponent below $1/6$ in two dimensions and below $1/24$ in three dimensions.
☆ Rigidity in the Lichnerowicz inequality for word-length semigroups
Melchior Wirth
We give an operator-algebraic characterization of Cayley graphs that are partial cubes, that is, embed isometrically into a hypercube. More precisely, noncommutative versions of the Lichnerowicz inequality control the spectral gap of the generator of a quantum Markov semigroup by the constant in the complete $Γ_2$-criterion of Junge and Zeng or the constant in the geometric Ricci criterion of Junge, LaRacuente and Li. We show that for word-length semigroups on group von Neumann algebras, equality in either of these inequalities occurs exactly when the Cayley graph is a partial cube.
☆ The distortion problem and orthogonality
Zhiyao Fang, Qi Liu
Schlumprecht [Israel J. Math. 76 (1991), 81--95] constructed an arbitrarily distortable Banach space. We further study distortion on this space under orthogonality constraints and obtain the following results. The exact distortion of his renormings is preserved in every infinite-dimensional subspace when the unit vectors satisfy both mutual Birkhoff--James and isosceles orthogonality for any finite family of equivalent norms. There are basic sequences of unit vectors satisfying both orthogonality conditions pairwise whose norms in the renormed space converge to the lower distortion endpoint. The proof combines finite-dimensional norm estimates with supporting functionals and the Borsuk--Ulam theorem. Further results concern finite and approximate Roberts conditions and an obstruction to simultaneous Pythagorean orthogonality for auxiliary norms.

☆ On the convergence of greedy algorithms in one-dimensional Wasserstein space
Geneviève Dusson, Carlo Marcati, Maximilian Penka
We study the convergence of the greedy algorithm for approximating a compact set by barycenters in metric spaces, in particular in the space of one-dimensional measures endowed with the 2-Wasserstein distance. To this end, we compare several metric $N$-widths, which measure the best error achievable with $N$-point barycenters, using either classical barycenters having nonnegative weights or signed barycenters, with weights of arbitrary sign summing to one. For the analysis we exploit that quantile functions embed the one-dimensional 2-Wasserstein space isometrically into a convex cone of $L^2(0,1)$, and barycenter sets correspond to nonlinear projections of convex or affine hulls. We prove, both in the algebraic and exponential case, that the convergence rate of the greedy algorithm using signed barycenters matches the one of the metric $N$-width defined with classical barycenters. We provide counterexamples showing that this fails for the other combinations.
☆ Stable phase retrieval from operator measurements
Deanna Needell, Yaniv Plan, Tomasz Szczepanski, Özgür Yılmaz
A known result of Cahill, Casazza and Daubechies [Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. Ser. B3(2016), 63-76] states that no frame in an infinite-dimensional Hilbert space does stable phase retrieval. We show that stable recovery becomes possible for more general operator measurements, but only at a single exponent. Given a system of bounded operators $\{A_j\}_{j\in J}$ on a real or complex Hilbert space $H$, we study recovery of $f\in H$ up to a global phase from the quadratic measurements $\langle A_j f,f\rangle$ and from their phase preserving square roots. We consider $p$-Bessel systems ($2\leq p<\infty$) for which we measure the quadratic data in $\ell_{p/2}$ and the square root data in $\ell_p$. In infinite dimensions, we show that whenever $p\neq 4$, no $p$-Bessel system of operators does stable phase retrieval. In the case of $p=4$, we show that stability still fails on any system of semidefinite operators. Nevertheless, we construct a system of rank-one operators, not all self-adjoint, for which stable recovery is possible. We also show that stability can be achieved on a system of self-adjoint operators of rank-two. For both types of measurements, we show that the stability can be tested on orthogonal pairs. This reduction preserves the optimal constant for quadratic measurements and, when the operators are semidefinite, for their phase preserving square roots. We deduce that in finite dimensions, uniqueness of recovery implies its stability. Finally, we show that whenever only the moduli of the measurements are retained, both the orthogonal reduction and the implication from uniqueness to stability can fail, already in dimension two. We also give second moment measurements in cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) as a motivation for the quadratic model.

☆ Norm-attaining operators on renormings of $c_0$
Manwook Han, Miguel Martín, Daniel L. Rodríguez-Vidanes
We study norm-attaining operators on three renormings of $c_0$: Read's space $\Read$, its smooth renorming $\sRead$, and Martín's space $\X$. We prove that, for every Banach space $F$ and every $Z\in\{\Read,\sRead\}$, norm-attaining finite-rank operators are dense in $\K(Z,F)$. Consequently, $\NA(Z,F)$ is dense in $\Lin(Z,F)$ whenever $F$ is reflexive. More generally, we establish that the compact Hilbertian smoothing construction of Debs, Godefroy and Saint-Raymond \cite{DGS} preserves the density of norm-attaining operators for all finite-dimensional ranges. We also extend a second-order criterion of Kadets, López-Pérez, Martín and Werner \cite{KLMWfr} from rank two to arbitrary ranks $k\geq 2$ for operators into $\ell_2^k$, and prove that the same smoothing preserves the existence and non-existence of such operators. We further investigate the possibilities and limitations of renorming techniques for excluding rank-two norm-attaining operators through analytical and geometrical approaches, including constructions that preserve the set of norm-attaining functionals. For Martín's space $\X$, we prove that, for every Banach space $F$ and every integer $1\leq k\leq\dim F$, there exists a rank $k$ norm-attaining operator from $\X$ into $F$, answering a question of Martín \cite{Mar}. We also show that, for every nonzero Banach space $F$, $\K(\X,F)$ contains a norm-dense linear subspace whose nonzero elements fail to attain their norms.

☆ A proof of the weighted Böttcher-Wenzel inequality conjectured by Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński
Tomoharu Suzuki
For a positive definite matrix $ω$ with two smallest eigenvalues $λ_1\leλ_2$ and the weighted Frobenius norm $\|X\|_ω^2=\mathrm{Tr}(X^*Xω)$, Mayumi, Kimura, Ohno and Chruściński conjectured that $\|[A,B]\|_ω^2\le\frac{λ_1+λ_2}{λ_1λ_2}\|A\|_ω^2\|B\|_ω^2$ for all complex matrices $A,B$. We prove this inequality for real and for complex matrices of every size, by a short computer-free argument, and we determine the cases of equality. In fact $\|XZY-YZX\|_2\le\|Z\|_{(2),2}\|X\|_2\|Y\|_2$ for all complex matrices of compatible sizes, where $\|Z\|_{(2),2}$ is the Ky Fan $(2),2$ norm (the $\ell^2$ norm of the two largest singular values), and the constant is attained unless $X$ and $Y$ are $1\times1$ matrices; the conjecture is the case $Z=ω^{-1/2}$. The best constant is the square of a unitarily invariant norm of $Z$, which is convex, so it suffices to treat weights whose $n-1$ largest eigenvalues coincide. For these, an inequality for one matrix and a pair of unit vectors, written in bases adapted to the pair of unit vectors, reduces the conjecture to the positive semidefiniteness of an explicit $4\times4$ Hermitian matrix depending on a $2\times2$ matrix $B$ in a convex set defined by two weighted operator-norm bounds, and an explicit determinant identity writes its determinant as a sum of products of factors that are visibly nonnegative; the phases of the entries of $B$ enter only through $|\det B|^2$, so the real case is literally a special case. As a second theorem we prove, for every weight, a strengthening of the conjecture that is equivalent to the inequality for one matrix and all pairs of unit vectors; its best constant is again a convex function of $ω^{-1/2}$, and the same argument applies. We also read the inequality as a sharp bound for inner derivations on the GNS space of a faithful state.

♻ ☆ Isomorphisms and representations of noncommutative function algebras
Marcel Scherer, Orr Shalit, Eli Shamovich, Mansi Suryawanshi
Let $V$ be a noncommutative (NC) variety in a NC operator ball. We study the dual operator algebra $H^\infty(V)$ of bounded NC functions on $V$, and the operator algebra $A(V)$ obtained as the closure of NC polynomials in $H^\infty(V)$. We identify the space of weak-$*$ continuous finite-dimensional representations of $H^\infty(V)$ as the similarity envelope $\widetilde{V}$ of $V$, and equip $\widetilde{V}$ with a metric which turns $\widetilde{V}$ into a complete invariant for $H^\infty(V)$, in the sense that $H^\infty(V)$ is weak-$*$ continuously isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if $\widetilde{V}$ and $\widetilde{W}$ are NC biholomorphic via a bi-Lipschitz map. Similar results are obtained in the completely bounded category as well as for the algebras $A(V)$ when $V$ is assumed homogeneous. In the case of homogeneous varieties $V$ and $W$, we obtain a sharper classification result, by which $H^\infty(V)$ is (completely) boundedly isomorphic to $H^\infty(W)$ if and only if there is a linear map which gives a bi-Lipschitz bijection between $\widetilde{W}$ and $\widetilde{V}$. The reduction to the linear case in the generality we work in depends on showing that the existence of maps implies the existence of origin-fixing maps, which we show using a novel ``two-circle trick" of independent interest. In the important case where the varieties are the full NC operator balls we find a striking rigidity phenomenon: if $A(B_E)$ and $A(B_F)$ are completely boundedly isomorphic then $E$ and $F$ are completely isometric. We also present a variety of examples illustrating the results and their sharpness, showing how several results from the literature fail to generalize to the setting studied here.

♻ ☆ On C*-nuclearity of graph operator systems
Adam Dor-On, Travis Russell
We classify the set of finite simple undirected graphs whose corresponding graph operator system is C*-nuclear. We prove that the operator system associated to the graph is C*-nuclear if and only if the graph is 2-chordal, as defined by McCullough. In particular, we present the first known example of a non-chordal graph whose graph operator system is C*-nuclear, as well as the first known examples of graph operator systems which are not C*-nuclear.

For a general class of uniformly superlinear integrands satisfying a $Δ_2$-condition, we establish existence and uniqueness of minimizers and derive a Fenchel dual problem with dual attainment and pointwise optimality conditions. We then specialize the framework to a logarithmic density whose correction is activated above a prescribed local gradient scale. For this model, we obtain explicit expressions of the Fenchel dual and optimality conditions as well as a pointwise radial formula for the dual proximal map involving the Lambert $W$-function. As the logarithmic parameter tends to zero, we prove equicoercivity and $Γ$-convergence to the ROF functional, together with convergence of the corresponding minimizers. Numerical illustrations indicate that the logarithmic correction can reduce staircasing for diffuse transitions, while retaining behavior comparable to ROF for sharp interfaces and a natural image.

Photoacoustic tomography is an emerging medical imaging technology whose primary aim is to map the high-contrast optical properties of biological tissues by leveraging high-resolution ultrasound measurements. Mathematically, this can be framed as an inverse source problem for the wave equation over a specific domain. In this work, for the first time, it is shown how, by assuming signal sparsity, it is possible to establish rigorous stable recovery guarantees when the data collection is given by spatial averages restricted to a sparse, randomly sampled portion of the boundary. Our framework encompasses many approaches that have been considered in the literature. The result is a consequence of a general framework for subsampled inverse problems developed in previous works and refined stability estimates for an inverse problem for the wave equation with surface measurements.

We propose a geometrization of compact metric spaces that is based on ideas of S. Banach and J. Mycielski. Then we prove the following conjecture of S. Banach and S. Ulam from 1935: in every compact metric space there exists a finitely additive probability measure, invariant under congruences. Moreover, our techniques allow us to solve a problem of M. Talagrand related to the Marczewski problem and the Banach-Tarski paradox with pieces having the property of Baire. We give also a very simple proof of the conjecture of Ulam about the product Lebesgue measure in the Hilbert cube and explain the existing results about congruence-invariant Borel measures in the language of our geometrization.

Despite progress in the rapidly developing field of geometric deep learning, performing statistical analysis on geometric data--where each observation is a shape such as a curve, graph, or surface--remains challenging due to the non-Euclidean nature of shape spaces, which are defined as equivalence classes under invariance groups. Building machine learning frameworks that incorporate such invariances, notably to shape parametrization, is often crucial to ensure generalizability of the trained models to new observations. This work proposes \textit{SVarM} to exploit varifold representations of shapes as measures and their duality with test functions $h:\mathbb{R}^n \times S^{n-1} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$. This method provides a general framework akin to linear support vector machines but operating instead over the infinite-dimensional space of varifolds. We develop classification and regression models on shape datasets by introducing a neural network-based representation of the trainable test function $h$. This approach demonstrates strong performance and robustness across various shape graph and surface datasets, achieving results comparable to state-of-the-art methods while significantly reducing the number of trainable parameters.

♻ ☆ Uniform Property (S)
William B. Johnson, Tomasz Kania
We introduce and investigate a quantitative version of Steinhaus' property$(S)$ for Banach spaces, called the \emph{uniform property$(S)$}. A Banach space$X$ is said to have uniform$(S)$ if for every pair of distinct unit vectors $x,y\in X$ and every $a>0$, the difference of the perturbed norms $$ \sup_{\|z\|\le a}\big|\|x+z\|-\|y+z\|\big| $$ is bounded below by a positive function of$a$ and$\|x-y\|$. We compute this modulus exactly for the spaces $L_1(μ)$ with atomless measure$μ$, $$ U_{L_1(μ)}(d;a)=\Big(\tfrac{4a}{2+d}\wedge 1\Big)d. $$ The class of spaces with uniform$(S)$ is stable under ultrapowers, Bochner-$L_1$ constructions, and contains all Gurariĭ spaces as well as Banach lattices of almost universal disposition. In particular, every Banach space embeds isometrically into a non-strictly convex Banach space of the same density having uniform$(S)$. We further exhibit an explicit equivalent renorming of$\ell_1(Γ)$, $$ \|x\|_S=\big(\|x\|_1^2+\|x\|_2^2\big)^{1/2}, $$ which endows$\ell_1(Γ)$ and all its ultrapowers with uniform$(S)$. These results settle, in ZFC, several open questions about the quantitative geometry of property$(S)$ posed by Kochanek and the second-named author.

We consider the nonlocal Schrödinger equation driven by a fractional Laplacian of order~$2s$, with~$s$ close to~$1$. Differently from the existing literature, which focused on either global problems in the whole of~$\R^n$ or Dirichlet conditions, we study here the case of nonlocal Neumann conditions in the halfspace. Moreover, we prove that ground states are nondegenerate, i.e. the only solutions of the linearized equation are linear combinations of the tangential derivatives of the ground state. Consequently, the ground state is unique, up to tangential translations and a change of sign.

An estimate of order $τ^3$ for the error of the approximate solution is proved under an assumption on the difference quotients of the computed grid functions on the first layers. The results are illustrated by numerical experiments.

Consider the motion of a rigid body moving into a viscous incompressible fluid that fills the whole space in 3D. The fluid motion obeys the Navier-Stokes system, while the motion of the body is governed by the Newton law. Both motions are affected by each other at the fluid-solid interface through the Navier slip-with-friction boundary condition, which is known as a substitution for the no-slip one to resolve the no-collision paradox. We adopt a monolithic approach and carry out the spectral analysis to deduce the large time behavior of the fluid-structure semigroup, where the shape of the body is allowed to be arbitrary. What is remarkable is that the decay structure is somewhat different under the full slip condition when the body is axially symmetric. If, in particular, the body is a ball, we then apply the linear theory developed above to the nonlinear initial value problem to show the stability of the rest state. It is, furthermore, asymptotically stable except for the full slip case.

More generally, if a fixed nonzero harmonic function on $\mathbb{Z}^3$ has $O(N^2)$ nonzero values in $Q_N$ along a sequence $N\to\infty$, then its support has a unique irredundant cover by finitely many characteristic planes. In this way, we prove that cross solutions converge strongly to a stationary solution on the limiting graph in a suitable sense. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this dimensional reduction recovers both vertex continuity and the Kirchhoff conditions.

In this paper, we introduce two auxiliary functions and reformulate our problem into two perturbation problems adapted to the structure of the system. This enables us to prove a result analogous to those obtained in previous studies, without assuming the differentiability of $b(t)$. The auxiliary functions are given by the differential equations $1+g'(t)=b(t)g(t)$ and $1-h'(t)=b(t)h(t)$, respectively. Our result shows that it suffices to assume $b\in C([0,\infty))$, $b(t)\asymp(1+t)^{-λ}$, and $|g'(t)|\lesssim(1+t)^{-(1-λ)}$ to obtain convergence to a diffusion wave.

Second, we introduce a new good unknown $Φ$, an effective total pressure gradient that combines the density, the temperature with the magnetic pressure. Although none of its constituents is dissipative by itself, we show that the coupling of $Φ$ with the divergence of the velocity and with the temperature produces dissipation for $Φ$ in all directions, together with an extra regularization of the divergence of the velocity. Combining these two mechanisms with new anisotropic commutator estimates and a hierarchy of time-weighted energy estimates, we prove that the system admits a unique global solution in $H^N(\mathbb T^2)$ for every $N\geq5$, and obtain a uniform-in-time bound on the highest-order energy as well as explicit algebraic decay rates. Even in comparison with the known result for the simpler isentropic counterpart, where the highest-order energy was only shown to grow at most algebraically in time for data in $H^{N}$ with $N\geq10$, our result removes the possible growth and lowers the regularity requirement to $N\geq5$.

We establish the propagation of chaos and derive the Vlasov equation from a many-body $N$-particle system in the mean-field regime with singular interaction forces bounded by $|x|^{-α-1}$ for $0\le α<(d-1)/2$ in dimensions $d\ge 2$, which in particular include the full range of sub-Coulomb interactions in three dimensions as well as the Coulomb interaction in two dimensions. Our proof is based on an energy-based framework for deriving weighted uniform bounds on cumulants that builds upon the recent duality method developed by Bresch--Duerinckx--Jabin in combination with a new Morawetz-type estimate, allowing us to remove the restriction to locally square-integrable interaction force kernels and handle more singular regimes.

☆ Large-scale regularity theory for optimal $p-$transport maps and application to concentration in the matching problem
Michael Goldman, Lukas Koch, Dario Trevisan
We consider the random bipartite matching problem between two independent families of uniformly distributed points in dimension three and higher, for the cost given by the $p$-th power of the distance. We show that, up to logarithmic factors, every moment of the displacement of the optimal matching is of the order of the typical interparticle distance. This is a higher integrability, or Calderón--Zygmund type, estimate for optimal transport, and it settles, on the torus and up to logarithmic factors, a recent conjecture of D'Achille, Mattesini and the third author. As a consequence, we obtain concentration of the matching cost around its mean for every $p\ge2$. The proof combines a deterministic large-scale regularity theory for optimal transport with $p$-costs, based on a harmonic approximation by a non-linear elliptic equation of $p$-Laplacian type, with tail bounds on local matching costs.

We study the nonlinear stability of viscous shock waves for the one--dimensional isentropic Navier--Stokes system with fast diffusion and singular viscosity. The waves connect a positive left state to zero specific volume at the right far field, where the density becomes unbounded and the viscous coefficient is singular. Under a vanishing--stress condition, we first establish the existence and uniqueness, up to a shift, of a monotone profile with an algebraic right tail. We then prove global existence and convergence to the profile for sufficiently small perturbations in weighted Sobolev spaces. The main difficulties stem from the singular nonlinear viscous term. We note that the existing approach for treating scalar conservation law with singular viscosity can not be applied to Navier--Stokes equations. We propose some new technique: after introducing an effective velocity and using an anti--derivative method, we establish unusual interactive--energy--estimates and thereby the expected energy estimates for velocity by coupling the two perturbation equations; furthermore, we introduce an auxiliary functional to eliminate uncontrollable terms. The artful weighted--energy estimates play a crucial role for treating singularity.

☆ Infinitely Many Plasma Echo Cascades and Sobolev Norm Divergence at the Gevrey-3 Threshold
Yue Luo
We construct a global solution to the confined Vlasov--Poisson system near a fixed homogeneous Penrose-stable equilibrium that exhibits infinite-time growth driven by nonlinear plasma echoes. For every sufficiently small \(ε>0\), the initial perturbation has size \(O(ε)\) in a Gevrey-3 norm with radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\). The corresponding solution is real and neutral, and the full distribution remains nonnegative. Its kinetic profile scatters in a lower Sobolev topology, while the spatial density and electric field decay. Nevertheless, the kinetic profile satisfies \[ \lim_{t\to\infty}\|f(t)\|_{H^{1000}_{z,v}}=\infty. \] The construction combines infinitely many well-separated echo cascades within a single global nonlinear solution. Each cascade generates a high-frequency output that persists under the subsequent evolution, and the accumulated outputs produce divergence in a fixed Sobolev norm. Thus, unlike finite-time echo amplification, the instability persists to arbitrarily large times despite scattering and macroscopic Landau damping. The construction identifies an instability mechanism at the critical amplitude-dependent Gevrey-3 radius \(λ_0\simeqε^{1/3}\), where cumulative echo amplification balances the initial Fourier decay.
☆ When and why can integral constraints improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks?
Myeong-Su Lee
Adding constraints obtained by integrating governing equations to the loss has been reported to improve the accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) in several applications, but mathematical understanding of these benefits remains limited. For several partial differential equations (PDEs), we derive stability estimates for losses with and without integral constraints. The comparison reveals that in certain parameter regimes, the standard loss has very weak control over specific error components, and that the integral constraints restore uniform control of these components. This explains when and why the constraints improve accuracy. Finally, numerical experiments support this interpretation. In parameter regimes where the standard loss is predicted to have weak control over those components, the two losses indeed show clear differences in accuracy. Conversely, in regimes where the standard loss retains sufficient control, both losses yield similar accuracy.

The coupling is not $C^1$ at the origin, so a direct Lyapunov--Schmidt reduction is unavailable, and the reduction has to be closed in a Lebesgue space although the matching requires $L^\infty$ control. We therefore solve a nonlinear outer problem by minimization, derive the dead-core property, solve the two scalar inner problems by a nonlinear contraction, match the inner and outer solutions, and close the scale and position equations by a Brouwer degree argument. This gives a Coron-type construction in the high-dimensional sublinear-coupling regime.

We prove that sufficiently strong Taylor--Couette flow yields a unique global strong solution whose density and concentration are uniformly bounded in time, without smallness assumptions on the initial cell mass or the fixed initial velocity perturbation. The main difficulty is that the angular shear tends to zero at infinity, so decay estimates on bounded regions do not directly control the full solution. To overcome this difficulty, radially weighted energy estimates exploit the radial velocity to control the density and vorticity at large radii. Combining these bounds with linear decay estimates and an energy comparison with the radial chemotaxis solution yields convergence of the density in $L^2$ to the radial solution with angularly averaged initial density, uniformly on fixed finite time intervals away from $t=0$ as the rotation amplitude tends to infinity. The decay of the radial solution then makes the full density small in $L^2$ at a finite time. An energy estimate preserves this smallness and gives global continuation.

This improves the previous quantitative lower bounds, which tend to zero as $|t|\to\infty$. The proof uses a positive measure representation of the Hamiltonian multipliers to sum the KdV Hamiltonians into an exactly conserved energy that controls the analytic norm.

Depending on these parameters, the wound may close completely or remain in a persistent state with a spatially nonuniform cell density. The model combines random cell movement, cell proliferation, and cell-cell adhesion within a finite sensing radius. We first derive the dispersion relation on the whole line and use it to compute the critical sensing radius and the corresponding wavelength. This relation shows that diffusion and cell proliferation stabilize the healed state, while cell-cell adhesion can make it unstable. On a bounded interval, the cell density is fixed at the healthy value on an exterior collar. In this setting, we establish conditions that keep the cell density within a positive bounded range, derive a sufficient condition for nonlinear exponential stability that depends on domain size, and formulate and numerically solve the associated linear spectral problem. The analysis shows how reducing the domain size can stabilize the healed state at parameter values for which the whole line model is linearly unstable. Finally, we compute critical sensing radii and domain sizes numerically and compare the sufficient stability bounds with the transitions observed in wound simulations involving perturbations of finite amplitude.

☆ Finite propagation speed for evolutionary equations
Joseline Simo Tekeu, Marcus Waurick
We study finite speed of propagation in the framework of evolutionary equations introduced by Rainer Picard in 2009. We establish sufficient conditions on the material law, which is represented by an analytic and bounded operator-valued function, and the unbounded spatial operator that ensure finite speed of propagation of information for solutions. Assuming a linear-in-frequency coercivity bound for spatially local material laws, we prove propagation on backward light cones for weighted $L_2$ solutions without a finite initial time, thus identifying hyperbolic-type evolutionary equations. The characteristic-speed threshold depends on the coercive coefficient and the principal spatial matrices, but not on bounded memory or delay terms or potential positive fractional temporal contributions. We illustrate the result with the scalar wave equation, Maxwell's equations, a fractional model in elasticity, and dual-phase-lag thermoelasticity.

☆ A dynamic variational principle on phase space for Wasserstein cubic splines
Gero Friesecke, Daniel Matthes
Wasserstein cubic splines have been introduced to provide a smooth interpolation in time between prescribed probability measures on $d$-dimensional Euclidean space. Their construction for $N$ measures is based on a multi-marginal optimal transport problem on a space of dimension $N\! \cdot \! d$, thus becoming very high-dimensional already for a small number of prescribed measures. We prove that the dimension can be reduced to a fixed number $2d+1$ via a dynamic variational principle on phase space. We also give an example showing that the Monge ansatz, which would also reduce the dimension to a fixed number, fails to capture exact solutions and is in general ill-posed, even for absolutely continuous measures.

Alessio Porretta, Davide Francesco Redaelli
We prove decay estimates for a large class of linear drift-diffusion operators with hypoelliptic structure. In the main example, the diffusion consists of (possibly superposing) local or nonlocal operators acting on a restricted set of variables, while diffusivity is transported to the whole space thanks to Hörmander-type conditions on the drift term. We prove both short-time and long-time oscillation estimates on the solutions, including bounded-to-Lipschitz smoothing in the sharp time scale and exponential decay, as time goes to infinity, whenever a strict supersolution, with the role of Lyapunov function, is supposed to exist. The estimates are proved with a unifying approach relying on doubling variables and coupling methods, using maximum principle in suitably time scaled moving frames. Applications range from nonlocal kinetic Fokker-Planck equations to heat conduction models in a chain of coupled oscillators.

☆ Source Conditions and Sharp Transition Asymptotics for the Factorization Method with Far-Field Data
George Pelekanos, Koung Hee Leem
The factorization method characterizes an obstacle through a range test, but practical implementations replace the associated Picard series by a regularized approximation. This paper studies the resulting regularization bias for inverse acoustic scattering by impedance obstacles. For a disc, we show that every positive-order Hölder source condition fails at each noncentral interior sampling point, whereas logarithmic source conditions hold uniformly on compact interior subsets for every exponent, with explicit constants. At the center, the bias decays linearly with the regularization parameter. We then derive sharp spectral transition asymptotics through the Lambert W function. These asymptotics determine the stabilization rate inside the obstacle, the iterated-logarithmic growth at the boundary, and the divergence outside. They also yield a threshold rule for which the reconstructed disc converges in measure, together with quantitative boundary-location estimates. For general impedance obstacles, we reduce the spectral decay of the symmetrized far-field operator to that of the data-to-pattern operator and obtain two-sided transition bounds in terms of the inradius and any radius larger than the circumradius. For a simply connected obstacle with analytic boundary, positive analytic impedance, and conformal center inside the obstacle, a Faber--Vekua normal form gives the sharp spectral law in terms of logarithmic capacity, with the same leading constant as for the disc. This class includes every convex analytic obstacle. Numerical experiments confirm the predicted spectral transition and illustrate its use in choosing the regularization level. The analytic normal-form result is proved only for a single boundary component.

For every $N\ge3$, the regular $N$-gon $R_N$ uniquely maximizes $Φ$, up to congruence, among simple polygons of fixed area with at most $N$ sides. The values $Φ(R_N)$ increase strictly with $N$. The maximization theorem answers Laugesen's question \cite[Problem~(1), p.~405]{ABLW} and proves the polygonal Szegő--Weinberger conjecture of Laugesen and Siudeja \cite[Conjecture~6.36]{LSH}. ♻ ☆ Finite-difference least square methods for solving Hamilton-Jacobi equations using neural networks
Carlos Esteve-Yagüe, Richard Tsai, Alex Massucco
We present a simple algorithm to approximate the viscosity solution of Hamilton-Jacobi (HJ) equations by means of an artificial deep neural network. The algorithm uses a stochastic gradient descent-based method to minimize the least square principle defined by a monotone, consistent numerical scheme. We analyze the least square principle's critical points and derive conditions that guarantee that any critical point approximates the sought viscosity solution. The use of a deep artificial neural network on a finite difference scheme lifts the restriction of conventional finite difference methods that rely on computing functions on a fixed grid. This feature makes it possible to solve HJ equations posed in higher dimensions where conventional methods are infeasible. We demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm through numerical studies on various canonical HJ equations across different dimensions, showcasing its potential and versatility.

We study positive solutions of the Dirichlet problem $-Δu = u^p$ in a uniformly convex domain $Ω\subset §^2$, $u= 0$ on $\partialΩ.$ For $p=1$, we assume that the right-hand side is replaced by $λ_1 u$, where $λ_1$ is the first eigenvalue of $-Δ$ on $Ω$ with zero Dirichlet boundary condition. ♻ ☆ A Sharp Planar Fractional Isoperimetric Inequality
Xiaosheng Lin, Dachun Yang, Sibei Yang, Wen Yuan, Yangyang Zhang
In this article, we prove the sharp form of the fractional isoperimetric inequality in the plane, originally posed by Maz'ya [Problem 1, Integral Equations Operator Theory, 2018]. More precisely, we show that, for any given $s\in(0,1)$ and any bounded domain $Ω\subset \mathbb{R}^2$ with $C^1$ boundary, $$ P_s(Ω) \le \frac{π^{s-\frac{1}{2}}Γ\left(\frac{3-s}{2}\right)}{s(1-s)Γ\left(\frac{4-s}{2}\right)}\left[\mathcal{H}^1(\partialΩ)\right]^{2-s}, $$ where $P_s$ denotes the fractional $s$-perimeter, $Γ$ denotes the Gamma function, and $\mathcal{H}^{1}$ denotes the $1$-dimensional Hausdorff measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. The constant is sharp and equality is attained by the disk. The proof proceeds in three steps: reducing the fractional perimeter to a chord functional, reducing connected domains to convex bodies, and proving the sharp convex chord inequality via a fractional Willmore-type inequality, a variational formula along outer parallel bodies, and asymptotic analysis.

♻ ☆ An inverse problem for semilinear elliptic equations with generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities
Pu-Zhao Kow, Rulin Kuan
We study the inverse problem of reconstructing the convex hull of unknown inclusions in semilinear elliptic equations with nonanalytic nonlinearities, by extending Ikehata's enclosure method to accommodate such nonlinear effects. To overcome the lack of the higher-order differentiability required for the Taylor-based construction, we construct an approximate solution based on the linearized equation through a first-iteration approximation. Under suitable structural conditions on the nonlinearity, we establish a reconstruction result for the convex hull of the inclusion. The method applies to a broad class of generalized Kerr-type nonlinearities that need not be analytic, without requiring an explicit formula for the nonlinear term. We also address the numerical challenges arising from the exponential decay of the CGO test data and show how they limit the accuracy of an implementation in double-precision arithmetic.

♻ ☆ Entropic metastability for drifted reflected Brownian motion: quasi-stationary distributions, regularity, and the exit position distribution
Louis Carillo, Lo{ï}s Delande, Boris Nectoux
Motivated by entropic metastability and the narrow escape problem, we investigate quasi-stationary distributions for reflected, drifted elliptic diffusions under mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions on a bounded domain. We address two problems, which are solved completely independently of each other. First, using purely probabilistic tools, we prove the existence and uniqueness of a quasi-stationary distribution under minimal regularity assumptions on the coefficients (the case of an unbounded domain is also analyzed). Second, using spectral theory and the theory of strongly continuous semigroups on L p spaces, we study the analytical properties of the quasistationary distribution. We relate it to the principal eigenfunction of the adjoint of the associated (non-symmetric) infinitesimal generator with mixed absorbing-reflecting boundary conditions, and we establish its regularity up to the interface between the two boundary parts. We also fully characterize the law of the exit point when the process is initially distributed according to its quasistationary distribution. In particular, we work on domains in which the absorbing (Dirichlet) and reflecting (Neumann) parts of the boundary meet tangentially, without forming any non-trivial angle, a configuration that raises genuine regularity difficulties for the solutions of the associated mixed boundary value problem.
♻ ☆ Low regularity potentials in heterogeneous Cahn--Hilliard functionals
Riccardo Cristoferi, Jakob Deutsch, Luca Pignatelli
In this paper, we study the prototypical model of liquid-liquid phase separation, the Cahn-Hilliard functional, in a highly irregular setting. Specifically, we analyze potentials with low regularity vanishing on space-dependent wells. Under remarkably weak hypotheses, we establish a robust compactness result. Strengthening the regularity of the wells and of the growth of the potential close to the wells only slightly, we completely characterize the asymptotic behavior of the associated family of functionals through a $Γ$-convergence analysis. As a notable technical result, we prove the existence of geodesics for a degenerate metric and establish a uniform bound on their Euclidean length.

♻ ☆ A Study of the PDE Model for the Anisotropic Consensus-Based Optimization
Keyu Li, Hui Huang
We investigate the nonlinear Fokker--Planck equation associated with anisotropic consensus-based optimization. Under suitable assumptions on the objective function, we establish global existence and uniqueness of density valued weak solutions for bounded initial probability densities with finite fourth moment. The main analytical challenge arises from the component-wise degeneracy of the diffusion, which vanishes along moving coordinate hyperplanes determined by the weighted consensus point. To overcome this difficulty, we develop spatial translation estimates based on weighted gradient bounds and uniform density estimates. Combined with temporal translation and moment estimates, these yield strong compactness in $L^2((0,T)\times\mathbb{R}^d)$ through the Fréchet--Kolmogorov compactness criterion, enabling passage to the limit in the regularized equations. Uniqueness is established through the associated McKean--Vlasov stochastic differential equation and Wasserstein stability of the weighted consensus point. Furthermore, we prove the propagation of $H^2$-regularity for sufficiently regular initial data.

We formulate a unified abstract framework for mean-field particle systems and their macroscopic limits from the perspective of differential equations and functional analysis. Combining semigroup theory with optimal transport, we study measure-valued evolutions directly through their generators, allowing different classes of mean-field models to be treated within a common structure. Specifically, the framework involves (1) formulating mean-field models abstractly using semigroups and generators; (2) establishing well-posedness of the corresponding nonlinear mean-field evolution equations in a class of solutions stable under approximation; and (3) proving quantitative propagation of chaos for the associated $N$-particle systems. The central tool is the transport derivative, which measures the infinitesimal variation of transport costs between Markov evolutions. We establish transport-stability criteria expressed through local generator inequalities and show how these criteria underpin both nonlinear well-posedness and particle approximation. When the generator's dependence on the law is controlled by averaged Hilbert-valued features, we obtain an $O(N^{-1})$ sampling contribution to the quadratic Wasserstein estimate through a variance argument. As an application, we obtain quantitative propagation of chaos for Lévy-type mean-field systems with state- and law-dependent drift, diffusion, and jump kernels under intrinsic transport conditions. The admissible jump kernels extend beyond those generated by multiplicative Lévy noise, demonstrating the scope of the abstract framework.

We give new proofs of interior second derivative estimates for the quadratic Hessian and Monge-Ampère equations with Dini continuous right-hand sides. Our approach uses a three-point maximum principle and requires no differentiation of the equations. For the quadratic Hessian equation, the estimate holds in every dimension $n\ge2$. For the Monge-Ampère equation, the proof is localised on sublevel sets of a strictly convex solution.

This type of NLEP appears frequently in pattern formation in reaction-diffusion systems. We show that on the even subspace, strict spectral stability holds exactly for $\Reγ>1$ when $r=(p+3)/2$. In the $γ$-plane, when $r>(p+3)/2$, two conjugate boundary arcs open to the left from $γ=1$, and the strictly stable region lies to their right. ♻ ☆ Geometric bounds for Steklov and weighted Neumann eigenvalues on Euclidean domains
Denis Vinokurov
We obtain sharp upper bounds for the first two nonzero Steklov eigenvalues among bounded domains in Euclidean spaces of dimension $d \geq 7$ under a natural normalization involving volume and boundary measure. These bounds are derived from a characterization of optimal domains and weights for the first two nonzero weighted Neumann eigenvalues. In dimensions $3 \leq d \leq 6$, we obtain upper bounds that are not sharp. We further establish strict upper bounds with sharp constants for all higher Steklov eigenvalues on simply connected planar domains with continuous boundary and finite boundary length. Beyond the second nonzero eigenvalue, these bounds were previously known only for smooth planar domains.

In this paper, we study the multiplicity of positive normalized solutions for the following Schrödinger equation with nonlinear point defects on a general metric graph $\G=(\V,\E)$, possibly with infinitely many edges \begin{equation*} \begin{cases} u'' = λu & \text{on every } \e \in \E, \\ \int_\G \abs{u}^2\, dx = μ& \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = -\abs{u(\vv)}^{p-2}u(\vv) & \text{at every } \vv \in \V_0, \\ \displaystyle \sum_{\e \succ \vv} u'_\e(\vv) = 0 & \text{at every } \vv \in \V \setminus \V_0, \end{cases} \end{equation*} where $p>2$, $\G$ is connected, $\V_0 \subset \V$ is nonempty, $μ>0$ is a given constant, $λ$ is an unknown Lagrange multiplie. For $p\neq4$, every fixed nonempty finite set $W\subset\V_0$ gives at least $2^{\#W}-1$ distinct positive normalized solutions, for every sufficiently small mass $μ>0$ if $p>4$ and for every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $20$ if $p>4$, and at every sufficiently large mass $μ>0$ if $20$ if $20$ if $p>4$. In the $L^2$-critical ($p=4$) case, under local conditions near the selected defect vertices, analogous results hold for masses slightly below $kq^2/2$, where $k$ is the number of these vertices and $q$ is their common degree.
comment: 82 pages. Comments and suggestions are most welcome
♻ ☆ Combined effects of evaporation, sedimentation and solute crystallization on the dynamics of aerosol size distributions on multiple length and time scales
Sina Zendehroud, Ole Kleinjung, Philip Loche, Lydéric Bocquet, Roland R. Netz, Erica Ipocoana, Dirk Peschka, Marita Thomas
We investigate three aspects of aerosol-mediated air-borne viral infection mechanisms on different length and time scales. First, we address the evolution of the size distribution of a non-interacting ensemble of droplets that are subject to evaporation and sedimentation using a sharp droplet-air interface model. From the exact solution of the evolution equation we derive the viral load in the air and show that it depends sensitively on the relative humidity. Secondly, from Molecular Dynamics simulations we extract the molecular reflection coefficient of single water molecules from the air-water interface. This parameter determines the water condensation and evaporation rate at a liquid droplet surface and therefore the evaporation rate of aqueous droplets. We find the reflection of water to be negligible at room temperature but to rise significantly at elevated temperatures and for grazing incidence angles. Thirdly, we derive a thermodynamically consistent three-dimensional diffuse-interface model for solute-containing droplets that is formulated as a three-phase Cahn-Hilliard/Allen-Cahn system. By numerically solving the coupled system of equations, we explore representative scenarios that show that this model reproduces and generalizes features of the sharp-interface model. These interconnected studies on the dynamics of aerosol droplet evaporation are relevant in order to quantitatively assess the airborne infection risk under varying environmental conditions.

☆ Conditionally Euclidean distance matrices
Shivani Goel, Hiroshi Kurata
We introduce a new class of matrices called conditional Euclidean distance matrices in this paper. These matrices are a generalisation of Euclidean distance matrices. We develop the theory of conditional Euclidean distance matrices and show that these matrices represent the squared Lorentzian distance between points of a Minkowski space. We also highlight the connection of conditional Euclidean distance matrices with the representation of hierarchical data in machine learning and the theory of general relativity in physics.
☆ A constructive inverse for the Jordan-von Neuman operator on abelian groups
Dorian Popa, Mircea Dan Rus
For an abelian group $G$ and a real Banach space $X$, we study the inhomogeneous Jordan--von Neumann equation $\mathsf{Q}[f] = g$, where $\mathsf{Q}$ is the quadratic difference operator of the parallelogram law. We characterize the functions $g$ in the image of $\mathsf{Q}$ and, under a summability hypothesis, recover a solution explicitly by an iteration on the diagonal followed by a propagation argument; neither regularity of $g$ nor divisibility of $G$ is required. As a consequence we obtain a sharp stability estimate of Forti--Găvruţa type for the quadratic functional equation.
comment: 19 pages
☆ Perturbed, suprametric, and interpolative contractions are metric contractions
Firuz Kamalov
We show that the fixed point theory of perturbed metric spaces, b-suprametric spaces, and interpolative metric spaces reduces to the metric case. A mapping is a perturbed contraction with constant $λ$ if and only if it is a Banach contraction with constant $λ$ for a metric that dominates the exact metric. Thus the theorem of Jleli and Samet is the Banach contraction principle in a finer metric, and we show that this metric cannot be chosen equivalent to the exact one. We also show that the fixed point theorem claimed for perturbed Kannan mappings is false. A b-suprametric is a logarithmic transform of a b-metric with the same constant, and an interpolative metric is a power of a metric with an explicit exponent, which is optimal for $α= 1/2$. Consequently, contractive conditions of maximum type in these spaces are equivalent to the same conditions in b-metric and metric spaces.
☆ Spectral isometries and invertibility preservers on Banach algebras
Zakariae Aznay, Fadil Chabbabi
We prove that every unital surjective complex-linear spectral isometry between complex unital semisimple Banach algebras is a Jordan isomorphism, thereby giving an affirmative answer to the spectrum-preserving form of Kaplansky's conjecture. We also characterize surjective complex-linear maps between arbitrary unital Banach algebras that preserve invertibility in either direction, satisfy either spectral inclusion, or preserve the spectral radius. In particular, for a complex-linear bijection between semisimple Banach algebras, preservation of invertibility in either direction implies preservation in both directions, and either spectral inclusion implies equality of spectra, even without assuming unitality. As an application, we study preservers of the Fredholm essential spectrum and essential spectral radius.
